heuristics.rule: All publicly advertised job postings in BC must include the expected salary or wage range
heuristics.condition: When an employer in British Columbia publicly advertises a job posting for any position where pay can be defined as a range
heuristics.action: Employer must include the expected salary or wage range in the posting
heuristics.because: Required under Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18; non-compliance can result in Director of Employment Standards investigation and orders to pay compensation
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18 — effective November 1, 2023 (phased by employer size)

heuristics.rule: Employers must pay H-1B workers at least the prevailing wage for the relevant occupation and location
heuristics.condition: When an employer files an H-1B petition for a foreign worker
heuristics.action: Employer must pay at or above the DOL prevailing wage determined by SOC code, MSA, and wage level
heuristics.because: INA Section 212(n) requires prevailing wage compliance as a condition of H-1B approval
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) Section 212(n); Title 20 CFR Part 655

heuristics.rule: BC employers cannot ask about an applicant's pay history at any point in the hiring process and cannot use pay history to set starting wages
heuristics.condition: When a BC employer is conducting any stage of the hiring process for any applicant
heuristics.action: Employer must not ask about prior salary or use pay history to set starting wages; must not retaliate against employees who discuss pay with coworkers
heuristics.because: Salary history ban is explicitly built into the Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18; violations are subject to enforcement by the Director of Employment Standards

heuristics.rule: Prevailing wage level (I–IV) is determined by job complexity and supervision, not by salary amount
heuristics.condition: When an employer assigns a wage level to an H-1B or PERM filing
heuristics.action: The wage level must reflect the actual job duties — Level IV requires high complexity, advanced expertise, and minimal supervision; Level I requires only basic understanding and close supervision
heuristics.because: DOL defines each level by occupational complexity and supervision criteria, not by the compensation the employer wishes to pay
heuristics.regulatory_basis: DOL Prevailing Wage Program; 20 CFR Part 655

heuristics.rule: BC employer size phase-in: 1,000+ employees required from November 1, 2023; 300–999 from January 1, 2024; 50–299 from January 1, 2025; all employers (no minimum) from January 1, 2026
heuristics.condition: When determining whether a BC employer must include salary ranges in job postings
heuristics.action: Apply the phase-in date corresponding to the employer's headcount to determine compliance obligation start date
heuristics.because: Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18 sets staggered implementation thresholds by employer size

heuristics.rule: Under the wage-weighted lottery rule effective February 27, 2026, Level IV filings receive 4 lottery entries vs. 1 entry for Level I
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B cap-subject petition is filed on or after February 27, 2026
heuristics.action: Employer must file at the appropriate wage level; each wage level grants a different number of lottery entries (Level I = 1, Level II = 2, Level III = 3, Level IV = 4)
heuristics.because: Federal Register 2025-23853 finalizes a wage-weighted lottery system to prioritize higher-wage H-1B beneficiaries

heuristics.rule: Ontario employers with 25 or more employees must include the compensation range (or fixed salary) in job postings for Ontario-based roles, effective January 1, 2026
heuristics.condition: When an Ontario employer with 25+ employees posts a public-facing or internal job posting visible to current employees, on or after January 1, 2026
heuristics.action: Include the expected compensation range or fixed salary in the job posting
heuristics.because: Required under Working for Workers Four Act, 2024, S.O. 2024, c. 15, Schedule 2; failure to comply can result in compliance orders and penalties from an Employment Standards Officer
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Working for Workers Four Act, 2024, S.O. 2024, c. 15, Schedule 2

heuristics.rule: Employers may substitute an independent authority wage survey in place of OEWS-based prevailing wage if they believe OEWS data is unrepresentative
heuristics.condition: When the employer files an LCA and believes OEWS data does not accurately reflect the local wage for the occupation
heuristics.action: Employer may submit an independent wage survey as the prevailing wage basis
heuristics.because: DOL Prevailing Wage Program permits 'independent authority' wage as an alternative to the OEWS-derived wage
heuristics.regulatory_basis: DOL Foreign Labor Certification Prevailing Wage Program; 20 CFR Part 655

heuristics.rule: Ontario does not include a salary history ban; asking about previous pay remains legally permissible in Ontario
heuristics.condition: When an Ontario employer asks a candidate about their salary history during the hiring process
heuristics.action: No legal prohibition applies; the Working for Workers Four Act, 2024 does not ban salary history questions
heuristics.because: The Ontario legislation does not include a salary history ban as explicitly as BC; the question is legally permissible under Ontario law
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Working for Workers Four Act, 2024, S.O. 2024, c. 15, Schedule 2

heuristics.rule: For PERM labor certification, the offered wage must meet the prevailing wage at both the time of PERM filing and at the time the worker receives the visa
heuristics.condition: When an employer files a PERM application for permanent residence sponsorship
heuristics.action: The offered wage must satisfy the prevailing wage determination at two points in time: PERM filing and visa issuance
heuristics.because: PERM prevailing wage requirements extend through the point of visa receipt, not just the filing date
heuristics.regulatory_basis: DOL Prevailing Wage Program; PERM regulations under 20 CFR Part 656

heuristics.rule: PEI pay transparency legislation requires job postings to include wage or salary range for employers with 10 or more employees
heuristics.condition: When a PEI employer with 10+ employees advertises a job posting
heuristics.action: Include the wage or salary range in the posting
heuristics.because: PEI Pay Transparency Act requirement

heuristics.rule: The FLC Data Center (flcdatacenter.com) is the authoritative source for current prevailing wage thresholds; values must be verified before filing
heuristics.condition: When preparing any H-1B or PERM wage determination
heuristics.action: Look up current OEWS-based wage using: FLC Data Center → select year → select state → select MSA → select SOC code
heuristics.because: DOL prevailing wage thresholds are updated annually when BLS updates OEWS data; prior-year values may be incorrect
heuristics.regulatory_basis: DOL Foreign Labor Certification Online Wage Library; OEWS survey (BLS)

heuristics.rule: BC employers above certain sizes must post annual pay transparency reports showing gender and other pay gap data
heuristics.condition: When a BC employer meets the relevant size threshold: 1,000+ employees (required from November 2023); 300–999 (from November 2024); 50–299 (from November 2025)
heuristics.action: Post annual pay transparency report with gender and other pay gap data, filed with the government
heuristics.because: Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18 imposes employer-side annual reporting obligations beyond job posting requirements

heuristics.rule: Canada's pay transparency legislation is at the provincial level only; there is no single national pay transparency law requiring salary disclosure in job postings
heuristics.condition: When advising a candidate on whether pay transparency rules apply to a Canadian employer
heuristics.action: Determine which province the role is based in and apply the relevant provincial legislation; do not assume a national standard exists
heuristics.because: As of 2025–2026, only BC, Ontario, and PEI have enacted substantive pay transparency requirements; Alberta and Quebec have not enacted comparable job posting transparency laws
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Pay Transparency Act SBC 2023 c.18; Working for Workers Four Act 2024 S.O. 2024 c.15 Schedule 2; PEI Pay Transparency Act

heuristics.rule: When negotiating salary as an H-1B candidate, identify the exact dollar threshold between your current wage level and the next one, then anchor your salary request to that threshold
heuristics.condition: When you are an H-1B candidate and your current offer sits at Wage Level II or III...
heuristics.action: ...research the DOL prevailing wage thresholds for your specific SOC code and geographic area, then frame your salary request as 'To qualify for Wage Level III/IV, my salary needs to be at least X for this occupation in this location'
heuristics.because: This argument is structurally independent of market data and ties the salary request to a concrete immigration benefit — moving from 2 to 3 lottery entries is a 50% increase in selection probability, which is quantifiable value the employer can understand

heuristics.rule: Never disclose current salary before an offer is made — it can only anchor the negotiation downward
heuristics.condition: When any employer asks for your current or past compensation at any stage of the hiring process
heuristics.action: Redirect with: 'I prefer not to share my salary history, but I'm happy to discuss my compensation expectations for this role.'
heuristics.because: Disclosing a below-market salary gives the employer a ceiling to work from rather than their actual budget, structurally disadvantaging you in every subsequent negotiation step

heuristics.rule: Use Canadian-specific salary sources (Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA) — never US sources — when negotiating Canadian offers
heuristics.condition: When negotiating a salary offer for a tech role in Canada...
heuristics.action: ...anchor to Robert Half Canada ranges and Glassdoor CA medians, not levels.fyi US or Glassdoor US
heuristics.because: US benchmarks are 25–40% higher in USD terms and will either cause you to anchor too high (seeming out of touch) or too low (leaving money on the table at Canadian ceiling)

heuristics.rule: Use lottery-risk avoidance as a retention argument once you are already on an approved H-1B at Level III or IV
heuristics.condition: When negotiating a raise or retention package as an existing H-1B employee at Wage Level III or IV...
heuristics.action: ...frame the turnover cost argument explicitly: replacing you means re-entering the weighted lottery with no guaranteed selection, representing a 50%+ probability of failing to hire the replacement at all
heuristics.because: Under the wage-weighted system, the employer has already cleared lottery selection risk — replacing an existing H-1B holder means absorbing that risk again, which is a quantifiable and asymmetric cost to the employer

heuristics.rule: If you're a remote worker, your protections follow your physical location, not the employer's headquarters
heuristics.condition: When interviewing remotely with a company headquartered in a non-ban state while you live in a ban state
heuristics.action: Invoke your state's salary history ban protections — they apply to you regardless of where the company is based
heuristics.because: Colorado, California, New York, and others explicitly extend their bans to cover employees located in those states even when the employer operates elsewhere

heuristics.rule: At Canadian tech employers, negotiate signing bonus first — not base salary — because it is the most flexible component
heuristics.condition: When a Canadian employer says 'the band is set' on base salary...
heuristics.action: ...shift negotiation to signing bonus rather than continuing to push on base
heuristics.because: Canadian offers have narrower negotiating bands (3–10%) than US (10–20%), and employers at established companies often genuinely cannot move the base but have more discretion on signing

heuristics.rule: Treat each salary dollar as worth more than face value if it pushes you across a wage level threshold
heuristics.condition: When an H-1B candidate is close to a wage level boundary (e.g., $15,000–$30,000 away from Level III)...
heuristics.action: ...prioritize closing that gap over negotiating equivalent amounts elsewhere in the comp package (e.g., signing bonus), because the marginal immigration value of crossing the threshold exceeds the dollar value alone
heuristics.because: A wage level increase buys both purchasing power and a structurally higher lottery selection probability — a dual return that US citizen candidates do not receive from the same salary increase

heuristics.rule: Use posted pay ranges as an opening anchor, not a ceiling
heuristics.condition: When a company is required to post salary ranges in job listings (California, Colorado, NY, etc.) and has done so
heuristics.action: Open with: 'I see the range is $X–$Y. Given my experience, I'm targeting the upper end of that range'
heuristics.because: A posted range tells you the actual budget; targeting the top of the range with justification is more powerful than guessing and more credible than demanding above range

heuristics.rule: When comparing a Calgary offer to a Toronto/Vancouver offer, add 8–12% to the Calgary gross salary before comparing take-home
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a tech job offer in Calgary (Alberta) vs. Ontario or BC...
heuristics.action: ...adjust for Alberta's zero provincial income tax, which increases effective take-home by approximately 8–12% on the same gross
heuristics.because: A CAD $130,000 gross in Calgary yields materially more take-home than the same gross in Toronto or Vancouver due to the absence of provincial income tax

heuristics.rule: If you already disclosed your salary, immediately reframe toward forward-looking expectations rather than defending the number
heuristics.condition: When you've already shared a below-market number — whether voluntarily or before knowing your rights
heuristics.action: In the next conversation, pivot: 'Now that we've discussed the role in more detail, I'm focused on [target range] for the offer' or cite market data to reframe
heuristics.because: Anchors can be disrupted by introducing new information or reframing the context; sitting passively on a low anchor compounds its damage across the entire offer

heuristics.rule: At FAANG Canada (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Shopify), expect total comp to significantly exceed base — negotiate RSU grants and refresh schedules, not just base
heuristics.condition: When negotiating at a large tech employer in Canada that offers RSUs...
heuristics.action: ...evaluate and negotiate total comp including RSU vesting schedules, not just base salary
heuristics.because: Senior SWE total comp at FAANG Canada ($175K–$260K+ CAD) can exceed base ($145K–$185K) by 30–50%, making base-only negotiation leave significant value uncaptured

heuristics.rule: Document any salary history question asked in a ban state — date, interviewer, exact wording — before deciding how to respond
heuristics.condition: When an employer in a ban-state asks about your salary history despite the legal prohibition
heuristics.action: Document the violation immediately, then decide whether to escalate; the violation itself can become negotiation leverage
heuristics.because: Private rights to sue exist in California, Colorado, Illinois, Massachusetts, New York, and Washington, with remedies including back pay, wage differentials, and civil penalties up to $25,000

heuristics.rule: Discount Montreal salaries by 15–25% versus Toronto when comparing raw numbers, then partially offset for lower cost of living
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a Montreal tech offer against a Toronto benchmark...
heuristics.action: ...recognize the posted salary will be 15–25% lower than Toronto equivalents, but factor in lower Montreal cost of living before concluding it's a worse deal
heuristics.because: Montreal's lower salary market is structural (bilingual requirements, different labor market) but cost of living partially compensates, so direct gross salary comparison overstates the real gap

heuristics.rule: Negotiate as a Canadian citizen in terms of mobility leverage when on PGWP
heuristics.condition: When you hold a Post-Graduation Work Permit (open work permit)...
heuristics.action: ...do not concede negotiation leverage based on immigration status; treat yourself as fully mobile
heuristics.because: PGWP is an open work permit — you can work for any employer without employer sponsorship, giving you the same walk-away power as a citizen

heuristics.rule: Counter 10–20% above initial offer as a baseline when you have no competing offer
heuristics.condition: When you have a single offer and the initial offer is at or near market rate
heuristics.action: Counter 10–12% above initial to leave room for the company to 'meet in the middle' at 5–8% above initial
heuristics.because: Recruiters are trained to move toward the middle — anchoring above your target lets the company feel they won while you land at your actual number

heuristics.rule: Don't negotiate an internal promotion without an external offer unless you're willing to accept a slower, weaker outcome
heuristics.condition: When pursuing an internal promotion salary negotiation...
heuristics.action: ...obtain a real competing external offer before initiating the negotiation
heuristics.because: Without an external offer, the company knows your reservation price, the status quo is the default, and managers can delay or partially deliver without consequences

heuristics.rule: Counter at 10–20% above the initial offer in round one
heuristics.condition: When you receive an initial offer and are preparing your first counter
heuristics.action: Ask for 10–20% above the initial number as your opening counter
heuristics.because: Companies typically move 40–60% toward your ask in round one, so anchoring higher gives you room to land at your actual target

heuristics.rule: Never give a number first — always redirect to their budget range
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter asks for your salary expectations or current compensation before an offer is made...
heuristics.action: ...deflect with enthusiasm and ask what the budgeted range is for the role
heuristics.because: Their number is almost always more useful than anchoring with yours — you risk leaving money on the table or pricing yourself out unnecessarily

heuristics.rule: Negotiate non-cash levers in priority order, not all at once
heuristics.condition: When you have multiple things you want from an offer...
heuristics.action: ...sequence asks: base salary and equity first, then signing bonus, then non-cash levers, then nice-to-haves last
heuristics.because: Negotiating everything simultaneously signals extraction-maximizing behavior; sequenced asks signal principled, specific priorities

heuristics.rule: Negotiate clawback terms before signing, not when you're trying to leave
heuristics.condition: When you receive a job offer with a signing bonus attached
heuristics.action: Treat clawback terms as negotiable contract points — structure, period, gross/net, and termination triggers — and address them all before you sign
heuristics.because: Once you sign, you have no leverage. All four terms have legitimate counteroffers that reputable companies will consider

heuristics.rule: Do not disclose visa/sponsorship status before the company has decided they want you
heuristics.condition: When applying or in early interviews as an international student requiring sponsorship...
heuristics.action: ...avoid proactively mentioning OPT/H-1B status unless explicitly asked; research sponsorship capacity through H-1B data and alumni intelligence instead
heuristics.because: Sponsorship cost becomes an elimination filter before your qualifications are weighed — disclosing early raises costs before benefits are established

heuristics.rule: Never name a salary number first — the first number anchors the entire negotiation
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter or HR form asks you to state your salary expectations or current compensation
heuristics.action: Deflect with 'I'm more focused on fit right now — if we're right for each other, we can be flexible on numbers' or enter $1 on forms to proceed
heuristics.because: Whoever names first sets the ceiling for their own outcome; if you name low, the company accepts and you leave money on the table; if you name high without knowing their range, you may anchor awkwardly

heuristics.rule: Never name a number or give a yes/no on the first offer call
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter presents an offer and expects a response on the call
heuristics.action: Ask clarifying questions about level, vesting, bonus target, and equity cliff, then request a few days to consider before reconnecting
heuristics.because: You lose negotiating leverage the moment you accept or anchor a number; delay preserves all options and signals deliberateness

heuristics.rule: Never volunteer future LMIA dependency concerns during negotiation
heuristics.condition: When you are a PGWP holder negotiating a first offer or raise...
heuristics.action: ...do not mention concerns about future PR pathways or LMIA needs
heuristics.because: Disclosing future immigration dependency signals to the employer that they have leverage over you, weakening your negotiating position even when that leverage may not actually exist yet

heuristics.rule: Counter 20–25% above initial when the offer is more than 15% below the levels.fyi median
heuristics.condition: When the initial offer is significantly below market rate
heuristics.action: Justify the counter with specific market data from levels.fyi framed as market alignment, not personal need
heuristics.because: A data-anchored counter is harder to dismiss and reframes the ask from 'I want more' to 'here's what the market looks like'

heuristics.rule: Negotiate promotion compensation before accepting the promotion, not after
heuristics.condition: When a company signals they are considering you for an internal promotion...
heuristics.action: ...say 'I'd like to discuss compensation for the new level' before the promotion is finalized
heuristics.because: Once you've accepted the promotion, your leverage disappears — the company has already achieved their goal of keeping you in the new role

heuristics.rule: If base feels locked, shift to signing bonus or equity
heuristics.condition: When the company signals the base salary is at its ceiling but negotiation isn't fully resolved
heuristics.action: Move the conversation to signing bonus, equity, or other levers instead of continuing to push base
heuristics.because: Different budget pools exist for different comp components; what's frozen in one lever may be available in another

heuristics.rule: Never accept or reject a verbal offer on the spot
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter delivers a verbal offer during a call...
heuristics.action: ...express enthusiasm, request the formal written offer, and set a 24–48 hour review window
heuristics.because: You need time to compare to market data and the act of reviewing is not a negotiation — it creates no friction while buying you leverage time

heuristics.rule: Signing bonus is the fallback lever, not the opening ask
heuristics.condition: When salary is fixed or at the top of a band...
heuristics.action: ...exhaust salary and equity negotiation first, then pivot to signing bonus as the gap-closer
heuristics.because: Signing bonus comes from a different budget than payroll and doesn't trigger salary band violations, making it available even when base is capped

heuristics.rule: Push for prorated clawback over cliff clawback
heuristics.condition: When a signing bonus agreement defaults to a cliff structure (full repayment if you leave before the period ends)
heuristics.action: Request prorated repayment language — 'a prorated structure is fair to both parties'
heuristics.because: Cliff structures create a binary risk where leaving even one month early costs you the full amount; prorated structures limit downside proportionally

heuristics.rule: Negotiate salary using market data, never personal need or visa-adjusted pricing
heuristics.condition: When countering an offer as a visa holder...
heuristics.action: ...ground the counter in levels.fyi, H-1B salary data, and peer compensation ranges rather than personal financial needs or immigration constraints
heuristics.because: Disclosing your reservation price or framing requests around personal need reveals your floor and eliminates negotiating room

heuristics.rule: Only negotiate compensation after the company has reached 'Yes-If' status — not while still in 'No-But' evaluation
heuristics.condition: When you are still in interview or evaluation stages and a recruiter tries to discuss compensation
heuristics.action: Defer with 'I look forward to receiving your offer' — signal that comp discussion comes after the hiring decision, not during it
heuristics.because: Negotiating while the company is still deciding whether to hire you forces excessive compromise; once they've decided they want you, leverage shifts substantially in your favor

heuristics.rule: Value early-stage startup equity at $0 for financial planning purposes
heuristics.condition: When evaluating a compensation package from a Seed or Series A company
heuristics.action: Base all financial modeling on cash salary only and treat equity as a lottery ticket
heuristics.because: 80-90% of startups fail and liquidity may never materialize; planning around equity claims leads to real financial miscalculation

heuristics.rule: Time CEC Express Entry application to achieve PR before PGWP expiry to eliminate LMIA dependency entirely
heuristics.condition: When you have a 3-year PGWP and a NOC TEER 0/1 job offer...
heuristics.action: ...accumulate 12 months of qualifying work, apply for CEC Express Entry, and target PR grant before PGWP expires
heuristics.because: Successfully executing this timeline means you never need an employer-specific LMIA, preserving full negotiation leverage throughout your early Canadian career

heuristics.rule: When you have a competing offer, counter to your target number directly — not 10–20% above initial
heuristics.condition: When you hold a competing offer
heuristics.action: Use the competing offer number as your anchor and ask the preferred company to match it
heuristics.because: The competing offer replaces the initial offer as the psychological anchor, removing the need to inflate your ask

heuristics.rule: Anchor internal promotion comp on market rate for the new role, not your current salary
heuristics.condition: When negotiating pay for an internal promotion...
heuristics.action: ...research and cite market comp for the new role level using external sources like levels.fyi
heuristics.because: Internal hires are systematically offered below market on the assumption they're 'already paid' — reframing to the new role's market rate counters this bias

heuristics.rule: Stop at round three; never push to round four or five
heuristics.condition: When you've already completed two or three rounds of back-and-forth
heuristics.action: Treat round three as the closing round and make your final ask there
heuristics.because: Pushing to a fourth or fifth round signals you're maximizing extraction rather than finding mutual agreement, damaging the relationship before day one

heuristics.rule: Give a specific number, not a range, when countering
heuristics.condition: When making a counter-offer on salary...
heuristics.action: ...state one precise target number rather than a range
heuristics.because: Ranges anchor at the low end — the company will interpret a range as permission to offer the bottom of it

heuristics.rule: Never accept verbal agreements on remote work — insist on written confirmation in the offer letter
heuristics.condition: When a company verbally agrees to remote or hybrid arrangements...
heuristics.action: ...require the exact terms in the offer letter before signing, not just email or verbal assurance
heuristics.because: Verbal agreements are unenforceable; 'we prefer remote' in an offer letter is legally and practically different from 'this role is fully remote'

heuristics.rule: Insist on net repayment language, not gross
heuristics.condition: When a clawback clause specifies repayment of the signing bonus without specifying gross vs. net
heuristics.action: Negotiate explicit language that repayment is calculated on the net amount received after taxes
heuristics.because: Gross repayment means you must repay money you already paid in taxes and no longer have — you can end up owing more than you ever kept

heuristics.rule: A higher salary negotiation is simultaneously a better H-1B lottery outcome post-2025
heuristics.condition: When negotiating compensation under the wage-weighted H-1B lottery system...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly frame targeting a Level III or IV salary as benefiting both parties — higher comp for you, better lottery odds for the company's investment
heuristics.because: Salary and immigration interests are directly aligned under wage-weighted lottery rules, making this a rare non-zero-sum negotiation argument

heuristics.rule: Treat negotiation as a fixed rule, not a situational choice — always counter at least once
heuristics.condition: When any job offer arrives, regardless of how generous it seems
heuristics.action: Counter or request at least one adjustment before accepting
heuristics.because: The worst-case outcome of negotiating is receiving the original offer unchanged; upside exists, downside does not — making it a pure expected-value positive action every time

heuristics.rule: Move to signing bonus or equity refresh when base salary is capped
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter says the base salary cannot be increased further
heuristics.action: Explicitly ask whether signing bonus or equity refresh is possible, framing these as alternatives to base
heuristics.because: Signing bonuses don't affect recurring payroll budgets and equity refreshes can often be approved outside normal comp bands, making them easier for managers to approve

heuristics.rule: Use LMIA investment as leverage in raise conversations with current employer, not in new job negotiations
heuristics.condition: When your current employer has already spent $3,000–$6,000+ on LMIA processing for you...
heuristics.action: ...invoke that investment as a data point supporting higher compensation in retention or raise discussions
heuristics.because: The employer's sunk cost in your work authorization is a credible argument for compensation alignment in an existing relationship, but has weak force in attracting a new employer who hasn't yet made that investment

heuristics.rule: Use precise numbers in late-round negotiation, round numbers early
heuristics.condition: When you are in round 2+ and both sides have narrowed, or when you have a specific data point to justify
heuristics.action: Switch from round numbers (anchoring signal) to precise numbers (research signal)
heuristics.because: Precise numbers like $192,400 signal you've done research; round numbers signal anchoring — each works best at different moments

heuristics.rule: Do not accept a retention counter-offer unless the root cause of your dissatisfaction is resolved, not just compensated
heuristics.condition: When a company makes a retention counter-offer after you reveal an external offer...
heuristics.action: ...ask yourself 'If this job paid what they're now offering, would I have stayed?' and decline if the answer is no
heuristics.because: 80% of people who accept retention counter-offers still leave within 12 months, and the counter-offer typically only buys the company time to find your replacement

heuristics.rule: 'Final offer' in an email still has room; 'final offer' on a phone call with a hard deadline does not
heuristics.condition: When the recruiter uses the phrase 'final offer'
heuristics.action: Assess the delivery channel and tone — if email, request a call; if phone with a deadline and matter-of-fact tone, treat it as genuinely final
heuristics.because: The phrase 'final offer' is often a negotiating position, not a hard limit, but context signals whether room remains

heuristics.rule: Express genuine enthusiasm before making any ask
heuristics.condition: When opening a counter-offer conversation...
heuristics.action: ...lead with specific, sincere excitement about the role before naming your number
heuristics.because: Enthusiasm signals good faith and keeps the tone collaborative rather than adversarial, which makes the recruiter more willing to advocate for you internally

heuristics.rule: Frame PTO negotiation as matching your current package, not asking for more than standard
heuristics.condition: When negotiating extra PTO days...
heuristics.action: ...anchor to what you currently have: 'I currently have 25 days — would you be able to match that?'
heuristics.because: Framing as matching avoids appearing greedy while giving the company a concrete, defensible reason to approve the exception

heuristics.rule: Any clawback clause that doesn't exclude layoffs is a liability trap
heuristics.condition: When reviewing termination trigger language in a signing bonus clause
heuristics.action: Require explicit language excluding 'termination without cause' and 'reduction in force' from clawback triggers before signing
heuristics.because: Sloppy or aggressive contract language can require repayment even after a layoff — leaving you owing tens of thousands when you didn't choose to leave

heuristics.rule: Reframe visa dependency as a retention differentiator, not a cost
heuristics.condition: When an employer treats sponsorship as a burden during comp discussions...
heuristics.action: ...explicitly state that H-1B holders stay 2–3 years minimum due to switching complexity, making them a long-term retention asset that justifies the salary requested
heuristics.because: This flips the power dynamic from 'I'm a cost because of my visa' to 'I'm a retention asset,' neutralizing the employer's implicit leverage

heuristics.rule: When salary hits a ceiling, pivot immediately to signing bonus or equity
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter signals that base salary cannot move due to pay bands or HR constraints
heuristics.action: Say 'If you could increase the signing bonus to X, I could accept this salary' — reframe the ask to a one-time cost
heuristics.because: Companies have asymmetric budget flexibility; signing bonuses don't affect ongoing payroll equity or pay-band precedent, making them easier for employers to grant while giving you equivalent real value

heuristics.rule: Use the final commitment close only once and only when genuinely ready to sign
heuristics.condition: When you have reached your target total comp number and are ready to commit
heuristics.action: Say 'If you can get to [X total comp], I'll sign today' as a binding commitment, not a negotiating probe
heuristics.because: This technique only works if it is credible; using it prematurely or insincerely destroys trust and eliminates its leverage effect

heuristics.because: The employer's leverage in this scenario relies entirely on the time-delay moat; GTS approval at a competitor eliminates that moat

heuristics.rule: Counter base first, then re-open equity separately after base is settled

heuristics.because: Mixing base and equity math in the first exchange muddies the negotiation and reduces your leverage on each component

heuristics.rule: After giving your number, stop talking

heuristics.action: ...remain silent and let the recruiter respond

heuristics.rule: Push for a title upgrade if the higher level puts you in a salary band with more upside
heuristics.condition: When a title upgrade is on the table at a large tech company...
heuristics.action: ...request the higher level code because it may trigger a re-evaluation that unlocks a higher comp band
heuristics.because: Level codes at large tech companies are directly tied to salary bands; a title upgrade can be a backdoor to comp increases that HR couldn't approve directly

heuristics.rule: Treat the signing bonus as locked capital for the full clawback period
heuristics.condition: When you accept a signing bonus with a cliff clawback structure you couldn't negotiate away
heuristics.action: Do not spend the full signing bonus until the clawback period clears — keep it liquid
heuristics.because: If you're laid off before the cliff, you must repay the gross amount immediately; not having the cash creates a serious financial crisis

heuristics.rule: Verify sponsorship execution capacity before signing, not just sponsorship willingness

heuristics.action: ...ask explicitly: do they have immigration counsel, have they sponsored before, what is their approval rate, who is currently on H-1B there, and get written confirmation before accepting
heuristics.because: Sponsorship willingness and execution capacity are different risks — a company without immigration infrastructure is a material risk regardless of intent

heuristics.rule: Proclaim a specific reason for every negotiation request to dramatically increase acceptance rate
heuristics.condition: When making any counter-request on salary, bonus, equity, or other terms
heuristics.action: Attach a concrete justification — student loans, relocation costs, market data — even if the reason is modest

heuristics.rule: Anchor counter-offers to objective third-party data rather than personal need

heuristics.action: Reference levels.fyi percentile data for the specific level and role at comparable companies as the basis for your range

heuristics.rule: Delay LMIA disclosure with startups until after receiving an offer

heuristics.rule: When base is locked, pivot to signing bonus as it doesn't affect headcount budget
heuristics.condition: When the company says base is fixed and cannot move
heuristics.action: Ask for signing bonus increase framed as bridging the first-year comp gap
heuristics.because: Signing bonuses come from a different budget than base salary, so companies have more flexibility even after declaring base is final

heuristics.rule: Calculate the hidden promo clock cost before accepting any internal transfer at the same level

heuristics.rule: Share the competing offer number but not the company name
heuristics.condition: When you have a competing offer and want to use it as leverage
heuristics.action: Disclose the dollar amount without naming the competing employer

heuristics.action: ...pivot explicitly to signing bonus as an alternative lever
heuristics.because: Signing bonuses come from a different budget, don't affect payroll or salary bands, and companies frequently have flexibility there even when base is locked

heuristics.rule: Negotiate relocation gross-up to cover the tax impact
heuristics.condition: When accepting a relocation package...
heuristics.action: ...negotiate the gross amount rather than the net figure, accounting for the fact that relocation assistance is taxable income
heuristics.because: Post-2017 tax law makes relocation assistance taxable, so a $10,000 relocation package may net only $6,500–$7,000 after taxes without a gross-up

heuristics.rule: A company refusing to add layoff exclusion language is a red flag about culture
heuristics.condition: When negotiating clawback terms and the company won't exclude termination without cause
heuristics.action: Treat this refusal as a signal about how the company uses clawbacks and weigh it as a data point about the offer
heuristics.because: Reputable companies have no legitimate reason to retain clawback rights over employees they chose to lay off — refusal suggests adversarial intent

heuristics.rule: Sponsorship cost does not justify below-market comp

heuristics.because: The actual cost of sponsorship is small relative to total compensation; treating it as a salary discount is a negotiation tactic, not a financial reality

heuristics.rule: Explicitly call out exploding offer deadlines — never let them silently expire

heuristics.action: Directly state 'This timeline doesn't work for me — I need time to make an informed decision and consult with my family'
heuristics.because: Virtually every exploding offer extends when called out explicitly; but silently assuming they'll still want you after expiry is a mistake — the extension only happens if you request it

heuristics.rule: Start processes with slow-moving large companies first, layer in fast-moving startups later
heuristics.condition: When running multiple interview processes simultaneously to generate competing offers
heuristics.action: Initiate Google, Amazon, Microsoft processes first (3-6 weeks), then start startup processes (1-2 weeks) so timelines converge
heuristics.because: Simultaneous offers maximize negotiation leverage; misaligned timelines force you to accept or decline before you have competitive data

heuristics.rule: Use specific salary range anchoring with market data sources in Canadian context

heuristics.rule: Stop pushing after 'final offer' if it meets 90%+ of your target, but probe signing bonus first

heuristics.action: Accept if it meets 90%+ of target, but first test whether signing bonus has 5–10% more room
heuristics.because: 'Best and final' often still has signing bonus flexibility even when base is truly locked, and pushing further without new leverage risks damaging the relationship

heuristics.because: Most companies have off-cycle adjustment mechanisms for documented gaps, but they are rarely proactively offered — you must initiate

heuristics.condition: Before you begin any salary negotiation
heuristics.action: Determine the specific number below which you will walk away, based on your current comp, financial needs, and non-cash factors
heuristics.because: Without a walk-away number you'll either accept something bad or overplay your hand; the BATNA is the anchor that keeps both mistakes in check

heuristics.rule: Negotiate on the phone, confirm in writing
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter is handling negotiations over email...
heuristics.action: ...request a 15-minute phone call before responding with any specific counter
heuristics.because: Recruiters batch and can easily decline email negotiations; on a live call they are actively advocating for you in real time, which is where movement actually happens

heuristics.rule: Close the negotiation with a specific, conditional commitment

heuristics.because: Clear, specific signals of good faith accelerate resolution and show you're negotiating in earnest, not endlessly maximizing

heuristics.because: Perceived lock-in is the source of employer leverage; knowing your legal rights converts a structural disadvantage into a negotiable constraint

heuristics.rule: Use an external decision-maker buffer to deflect immediate pressure
heuristics.condition: When a recruiter is pushing for a same-call decision or immediate commitment
heuristics.action: Say 'I'll review this and discuss with my family — I'll follow up if I have questions'
heuristics.because: Removes you from direct real-time pressure; the recruiter cannot demand an instant decision if the decision is not solely yours, buying you time without appearing uninterested

heuristics.rule: Always ask for the offer level, not just the total comp number

heuristics.action: Confirm which band level the offer is placed at and whether it is at the low, mid, or high end of that band
