decision_factors.factor: Province of the job posting
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pay transparency obligations vary by province; only BC, Ontario (25+ employees), and PEI have enacted job posting salary range requirements as of 2025–2026
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the role is posted for BC, Ontario, PEI, or another province; apply the corresponding provincial statute if one exists

decision_factors.factor: SOC code (Standard Occupational Classification)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The SOC code determines which occupational wage table applies; different SOC codes yield substantially different prevailing wage thresholds even in the same location
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Employer selects the SOC code that matches the actual job duties — e.g., 15-1252 for Software Developers, 11-3021 for Computer and Information Systems Managers

decision_factors.factor: Employer size (number of employees)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Both BC's phase-in schedule and Ontario's 25-employee threshold mean smaller employers may not yet be obligated to post salary ranges, or may not be covered at all
decision_factors.how_to_assess: BC: determine headcount to identify applicable phase-in date (1,000+, 300–999, 50–299, or all employers from Jan 1, 2026); Ontario: determine whether employer has 25+ employees; PEI: determine whether employer has 10+ employees

decision_factors.factor: Geographic area (Metropolitan Statistical Area)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prevailing wages are set by MSA; the same SOC code and wage level produce significantly different dollar thresholds across cities (e.g., Level I Software Developer: $121,430 in San Francisco vs. $86,340 in Austin)
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the MSA in which the worker will be employed; use FLC Data Center to look up wages by MSA

decision_factors.factor: Whether the posting is public-facing or internal
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Ontario's requirement applies to both public-facing and internal job postings visible to current employees, broadening the scope beyond external candidates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether the posting is visible externally or only to current employees; both types are covered under Ontario's Working for Workers Four Act, 2024

decision_factors.factor: Wage level (I through IV)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Wage level determines the minimum salary the employer must pay AND, effective February 27, 2026, determines the number of H-1B lottery entries (1–4) for the petition
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess against DOL criteria: Level I = basic understanding, close supervision; Level II = good understanding, general supervision; Level III = complex situations, independent judgment; Level IV = high complexity, minimal supervision, instructs others

decision_factors.factor: Presence or absence of a salary history ban in the relevant province
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether an employer can legally ask about salary history affects a candidate's negotiation strategy; in BC the question is prohibited, in Ontario it remains legal
decision_factors.how_to_assess: BC: salary history ban is explicit in Pay Transparency Act SBC 2023 c.18; Ontario: no salary history ban in Working for Workers Four Act 2024; assess province before advising on deflection tactics

decision_factors.factor: Employer's prior OFLC filing history
decision_factors.why_it_matters: DOL OFLC performance data discloses exact wages paid for prior H-1B filings by employer, occupation, and location — establishing a verifiable employer-specific wage benchmark
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search DOL OFLC Performance Data at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/eta/foreign-labor/performance for the specific employer, SOC code, and MSA

decision_factors.factor: Availability of employer pay transparency reports (BC)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: BC employers above size thresholds must file annual pay transparency reports showing gender and other pay gap data; publicly accessible reports may allow candidates to infer internal pay equity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the BC employer meets the relevant size threshold and whether their annual pay transparency report has been filed and is publicly accessible

decision_factors.factor: Annual BLS OEWS data update cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prevailing wage thresholds change annually; using outdated values may result in LCA filings that underpay relative to the current prevailing wage requirement
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Always verify against the current year's FLC Data Center before filing; do not rely on prior-year tables

decision_factors.factor: Current wage level classification (I–IV) of the offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines the number of lottery entries (1–4) and directly sets selection probability; the difference between Level II and III is a 50% increase in odds
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the employer's immigration attorney which wage level the LCA will be filed at, or independently look up the DOL OEWS prevailing wage tables for the specific SOC code and metro area

decision_factors.factor: Whether you are in a salary history ban state
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether you are legally protected from being asked about past compensation and whether you have legal recourse if asked
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the list of 22 states and 23+ municipalities; also check your remote work location, not just the employer's HQ location

decision_factors.factor: City / Province of role
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Salary benchmarks vary 10–25% across Canadian cities, and Alberta's no-provincial-income-tax rule changes effective take-home independently of gross salary
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Compare gross offer to city-specific benchmarks (Toronto/Vancouver as baseline); for Calgary/Edmonton add 8–12% take-home premium; for Montreal discount 15–25% but adjust for COL

decision_factors.factor: Proximity of offered salary to the next wage level threshold
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you are $10,000–$30,000 away from the next wage level, the immigration value of that increment is disproportionately high relative to its dollar value
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference the offered salary against DOL prevailing wage data for the role's SOC code and location to calculate the exact gap to the next threshold

decision_factors.factor: Whether the employer is required to post a pay range
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Posted ranges reveal actual budget and shift negotiating power to the candidate by eliminating information asymmetry
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check if employer meets employee threshold in states like California (15+), Hawaii (50+), Illinois (15+), Maryland (all), Minnesota (30+), New York (4+), Washington (15+)

decision_factors.factor: Employer type: FAANG Canada vs. mid-tier tech vs. enterprise
decision_factors.why_it_matters: FAANG Canada pays materially more in total comp (especially RSUs) than the broad market — mid-tier Canadian tech often pays near Robert Half ranges with no equity
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether offer includes RSUs; compare to FAANG Canada benchmarks (Amazon, Google, Shopify) vs. Robert Half ranges for non-FAANG

decision_factors.factor: SOC code and job duties classification
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Wage level is tied to duties and SOC code, not salary alone — a higher salary without matching duties does not automatically move you to a higher wage level
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review the job description against DOL wage level definitions; confirm with the employer's immigration counsel what SOC code and level the LCA will use

decision_factors.factor: Whether you have already voluntarily disclosed your salary
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Voluntary disclosure is explicitly exempt from ban protections; it cannot be legally contested after the fact, and creates a downward anchor
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review whether you brought up the number unprompted or whether they asked first; the legal protection only applies when they solicited the information

decision_factors.factor: Equity (RSU) structure and vesting schedule
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For senior roles, RSUs can add 30–50% above base salary; not negotiating or understanding them means treating a $170K total comp role as a $145K base role
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request full RSU grant amount, vesting cliff, annual refresh rate; compare to role-level benchmarks at FAANG Canada

decision_factors.factor: Whether the candidate is already on an approved H-1B vs. entering the lottery
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The weighted lottery rule only affects new lottery selection; existing approved H-1B holders are not retroactively affected, which changes the negotiation dynamic entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine current visa status: is this a first-time H-1B filing, a transfer, or a renewal? Only new cap-subject filings face the weighted lottery

decision_factors.factor: Which state law applies to your specific situation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some states (Michigan, Wisconsin) actively prohibit local governments from passing salary history bans, meaning there is zero protection even at the city level
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your physical work location, then check both state-level bans and notable municipal exceptions; do not assume a ban applies without verifying

decision_factors.factor: Pay transparency legislation (BC and Ontario, Jan 2026)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Posted salary ranges will become mandatory, removing information asymmetry and allowing candidates to see the full band before negotiating
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the job posting already includes a salary range (early compliers exist); if not, ask recruiter for the band directly

decision_factors.factor: Legal challenge risk to the final rule
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Court injunctions could delay or block implementation before the FY2027 lottery, making wage-level-based negotiation arguments premature or moot
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Monitor immigration law news sources for injunctions filed against the rule between publication (December 2025) and effective date (February 2026)

decision_factors.factor: Whether a private right to sue exists in your state
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a violation is enforceable beyond filing a complaint — and whether a violation gives you real leverage in negotiation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Private rights to sue confirmed in: California, Colorado, Illinois, Massachusetts, New York, Washington; other states may only allow labor department complaints

decision_factors.factor: Canadian vs. US immigration status and path to PR
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The Canada–US comp gap is severe at FAANG level (senior SWE: $161K USD Canada vs. $400K USD US FAANG), but US H-1B uncertainty and 134-year India-born green card wait changes the real expected value calculation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: For international candidates: compare expected compensation over 5–10 year horizon including immigration stability premium; Canadian PR achievable in 1–2 years vs. H-1B uncertainty

decision_factors.factor: Employer's cost basis for sponsorship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Employers who have already invested $3,000–$8,000 in fees and attorney costs for an existing H-1B employee face higher replacement costs under the new system, strengthening the candidate's retention leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you are an existing sponsored employee (high employer sunk cost + lottery risk) vs. a new hire candidate (lower sunk cost)

decision_factors.factor: Filing deadline for state labor complaints
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Missing the window eliminates your legal remedy entirely; deadlines range from 6 months to 3 years depending on state
decision_factors.how_to_assess: If you believe a violation occurred, check your state labor department's complaint deadline immediately — do not wait

decision_factors.factor: RRSP matching terms
decision_factors.why_it_matters: RRSP matching is a form of deferred compensation not captured in base salary; it affects total comp comparison across employers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request specifics on RRSP match percentage and vesting; include in total comp calculation alongside base and equity

decision_factors.factor: Whether the role is an internal promotion vs. new external hire
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some states' salary history bans only cover new hires, meaning internal promotion negotiations may not carry the same legal protections
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Washington's ban explicitly covers internal promotions; check whether your state extends the ban beyond external hiring

decision_factors.factor: Years of experience relative to role level benchmarks
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian salary bands are meaningfully different by seniority level (junior $65K–$95K vs. senior $120K–$165K); being mis-leveled down costs $25K–$40K annually
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Match your YOE (0–3, 3–6, 6–10) to published Robert Half Canada ranges for your role; flag if offer falls below median for your experience tier

decision_factors.factor: Work permit portability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether you can realistically walk away from an offer or employer, which is the foundation of all negotiation leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether your current or prospective permit is open (PGWP, PR) vs. employer-specific (LMIA-backed, intra-company transfer); open = full leverage, employer-specific = reduced leverage

decision_factors.factor: Distance of initial offer from market rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines how aggressive your counter should be — a below-market offer justifies a larger counter with market data as justification
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Pull levels.fyi data for the specific company, level, and location and compare to the initial offer

decision_factors.factor: Presence of a real external competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Transforms internal negotiation leverage from low to high by introducing a credible, time-bounded cost of inaction for the employer
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you have a written offer with a specific number and deadline? A verbal interest or recruiter reach-out does not constitute real leverage

decision_factors.factor: BATNA strength
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Your walk-away alternative determines how much pressure you can credibly apply; weak BATNA means the company can hold firm and you have no exit
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify your actual best alternative — current job, competing offer, or nothing — and honestly evaluate whether you would act on it

decision_factors.factor: Whether you have a competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A competing offer transforms negotiation from a one-sided ask into a bilateral decision the company must respond to — it provides concrete external validation of your market value
decision_factors.how_to_assess: You either have one or you don't — if you do, know the exact number and timeline attached to it before using it as leverage

decision_factors.factor: Budget ownership of the lever
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Different levers are owned by different budget holders — hiring manager may approve remote work while HR owns salary bands, making some levers easier to move than others
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself who needs to approve the specific ask; non-cash levers like pro dev budgets and remote work are often manager-level decisions, not HR committee decisions

decision_factors.factor: Clawback structure (cliff vs. prorated)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Cliff structures mean 100% repayment liability until the final day of the clawback period; prorated structures reduce liability proportionally over time — the same bonus carries dramatically different risk depending on structure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the contract language explicitly. Look for 'full repayment' or 'prorated based on months remaining.' If it doesn't say prorated, it is almost certainly a cliff.

decision_factors.factor: Company's H-1B sponsorship history and approval rate
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A company with no prior H-1B sponsorships or low approval rates represents a material risk that the offer is not executable, regardless of the salary number
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check public USCIS H-1B disclosure data, ask directly whether they have immigration counsel and current H-1B employees, and request confirmation in writing before signing

decision_factors.factor: Whether you have competing offers from companies you'd actually work for
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A real competing offer is the single most reliable source of negotiating leverage — it transforms your ask from opinion into market evidence and creates genuine optionality
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count active offers or imminent offers from companies you would genuinely accept; distinguish real competing offers from vague 'other conversations'

decision_factors.factor: Company stage and equity liquidity timeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Equity is 30-60% of total comp at large tech companies but may be worth $0 at early-stage companies; misvaluing this reverses offer rankings
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask for the 409A valuation, preferred share liquidation preferences, and estimated IPO or liquidity timeline; apply a discount rate based on stage (public=80-90%, Series C-D=60-90%, Seed/A=0%)

decision_factors.factor: Time remaining on PGWP relative to CEC eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If you can achieve PR before PGWP expiry, you never enter LMIA dependency; if you cannot, your negotiation leverage decreases as expiry approaches
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate PGWP expiry date, subtract 12 months of required CEC work experience, subtract ~6 months of Express Entry processing — determine if PR can land before expiry

decision_factors.factor: Competing offer leverage (BATNA)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Changes the entire counter structure — with a competing offer you counter to your target directly rather than anchoring above it
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether you have a written competing offer with a specific number you can reference

decision_factors.factor: Root cause of considering a move
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a retention counter-offer can actually resolve your dissatisfaction or just delay inevitable departure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'If comp were fixed, would I still want to leave?' If yes due to manager, scope, learning, or ceiling — comp alone won't fix it

decision_factors.factor: Presence of a competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A real competing offer is the single strongest lever in negotiation; it creates urgency, imports a deadline, and forces the target company to act
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you have a written or verbal offer with a specific number from another employer that you would genuinely consider accepting?

decision_factors.factor: Whether the negotiation is happening by phone or email
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Phone calls put recruiters in real-time advocacy mode; email allows easy, low-friction 'no' responses and loses nuance
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess the channel being used — if email, proactively request a call before counter-offering

decision_factors.factor: Whether the agreement is in writing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Verbal commitments on remote work, PTO, or other non-cash terms are unenforceable and often forgotten or reversed after joining
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the offer letter explicitly states the terms; if it only appears in email or verbal conversation, it is not secured

decision_factors.factor: Termination trigger language
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Whether the clawback applies only to voluntary resignation and termination for cause — or also to layoffs — determines whether you bear risk for things outside your control
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search the contract for phrases like 'for any reason or no reason,' 'voluntary resignation,' 'termination for cause.' Absence of layoff exclusion is not protection — it must be explicitly stated.

decision_factors.factor: OEWS wage level classification of the offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Post-2025, wage level directly determines H-1B lottery odds — Level III or IV gives significantly better odds, meaning the wage level affects both comp and immigration outcomes simultaneously
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Cross-reference the offered salary against OEWS wage tables for the job's SOC code and geographic location to determine which level it falls into

decision_factors.factor: Timing overlap of multiple active offer windows
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Leverage from competing offers only exists if offer windows actually overlap; a competing offer that expired two weeks ago provides no real pressure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Map interview start dates and typical decision timelines; start large-company interviews first (slower, wider windows) and startup interviews later (faster, tighter) to maximize overlap

decision_factors.factor: Option exercise window after leaving
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 90-day exercise window means you must pay to exercise vested options within 90 days of leaving or forfeit them; a 10-year window gives you flexibility to wait for a liquidity event
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask directly: 'How long after leaving do I have to exercise my options?'; standard is 90 days, best-in-class is 5-10 years

decision_factors.factor: Whether target or current employer is GTS-approved
decision_factors.why_it_matters: GTS reduces LMIA processing from 2–5 months to ~2 weeks, making competing offers from GTS employers practically usable as leverage rather than theoretical
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the GTS employer designation list or ask HR directly whether the company has previously used Global Talent Stream

decision_factors.factor: Exploding offer pressure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Time pressure reduces your negotiating room and ability to generate competing offers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the offer has a hard deadline and how much time you have to respond

decision_factors.factor: Promotion clock position
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines the true hidden cost of an internal transfer at the same level — it can add 2+ years to your next promotion eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: How many months into your current promo cycle are you? What is the company's minimum tenure before next promotion after a transfer?

decision_factors.factor: Where current total comp sits relative to levels.fyi median
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the offer is already at or above market median, there is structurally less room to push; continuing signals you are extracting rather than calibrating to market
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look up the role, level, and location on levels.fyi and compare the full offer package — base, equity, bonus — against the median

decision_factors.factor: Whether the base salary band is actually locked
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If base truly cannot move, knowing this quickly redirects your energy to signing bonus, equity, or non-cash levers that have real budget flexibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR directly whether the band is the constraint; test by asking about signing bonus separately even after being told base is final

decision_factors.factor: Clawback provisions on signing bonus and relocation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Signing bonuses and relocation packages typically require repayment if you leave within 12–24 months, which affects true value if you have any uncertainty about tenure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the offer letter or separate bonus agreement for repayment clauses; confirm the repayment period and whether it prorates over time

decision_factors.factor: Gross vs. net repayment obligation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Gross repayment means you repay the pre-tax amount, not what you actually received. On a $30K bonus with a 33% effective tax rate, you owe $10K more than you kept.
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Look for explicit 'gross amount' or 'net of applicable taxes' language. If it says gross, negotiate. If it's silent, treat it as gross until confirmed otherwise in writing.

decision_factors.factor: OPT expiration date and H-1B filing deadline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Timeline urgency changes negotiation posture — a student with 6 months of OPT remaining has more flexibility than one with 6 weeks, affecting BATNA credibility and process parallelism
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate exact OPT end date, STEM OPT extension eligibility, and the H-1B cap filing window (April 1 each year) to map your actual runway

decision_factors.factor: Whether the company has reached 'Yes-If' vs. 'No-But' status on hiring you
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Negotiating before the company has decided to hire you forces compromise; negotiating after they've committed gives you full leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you've received a formal or informal offer signal; 'we'd like to make you an offer' is Yes-If; 'we're still evaluating' is No-But

decision_factors.factor: Vesting schedule structure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 4-year cliff (all equity vests at year 4) versus quarterly vesting after a 1-year cliff is a massive practical difference in when you can access the value
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly for the vesting schedule; confirm whether there is a cliff, the cliff duration, and the post-cliff cadence (monthly vs. quarterly)

decision_factors.factor: Employer size and LMIA capability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large employers are more likely to have existing LMIA processes and legal resources, making them viable competing offer sources for candidates who need sponsorship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Target Amazon, Google, Microsoft Canada and established scale-ups for competing offers if you need LMIA; avoid relying on startups as LMIA-capable competing offer sources

decision_factors.factor: Company stage (startup vs. public company)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Affects which levers are flexible — equity is often more negotiable at growth-stage companies while base and signing bonus are more flexible at large public companies
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify whether the company is pre-IPO, growth-stage, or a large public tech company and adjust which components you prioritize

decision_factors.factor: Whether promotion is discretionary vs. criteria-based
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Discretionary promotions are subject to indefinite deferral; criteria-based promotions give you something concrete to negotiate around and hold the company accountable to
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask your manager: 'What specifically would I need to demonstrate, and by when, to get promoted?' Vague answers indicate discretionary

decision_factors.factor: Recruiter tone shift
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The recruiter's affect is a real-time signal of whether room remains; a shift from collaborative to administrative signals you've reached the ceiling
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Notice whether the recruiter is still problem-solving with you or has become transactional and matter-of-fact in their language

decision_factors.factor: Specificity of your target number
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Vague asks ('something closer to $200K') anchor less effectively than precise numbers ('I'm looking for $195K') — precision signals market research and confidence
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Before negotiating, research the role on levels.fyi or equivalent sources and commit to a single specific number

decision_factors.factor: Title's impact on future employer evaluations
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The title you accept affects the level at which future employers evaluate and comp you; a lower title can suppress offers even if your actual scope was higher
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check what level the equivalent role is called at peer companies; ask whether the title is what would appear externally on LinkedIn

decision_factors.factor: Clawback period length
decision_factors.why_it_matters: 12 months is industry standard; 18–24 months extends your liability window significantly and limits career mobility for longer
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify the stated period in the contract. Compare against the 12-month standard. Periods over 12 months are worth actively pushing back on.

decision_factors.factor: Quality and credibility of BATNA
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Without a real alternative — whether a competing offer, another degree program, CPT position, or another country's job market — counter-offers lack credibility and the employer retains leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify at least one path you would genuinely pursue if this offer fell through; a BATNA only works if you would actually use it

decision_factors.factor: Information asymmetry — what the company knows about your current salary and alternatives
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Your negotiating power is directly proportional to what the company does not know about your floor and alternatives; revealing your current salary or reservation price collapses that power
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Audit what you've disclosed: current comp, specific asks, how you rank this offer vs. others — each disclosure reduces asymmetry

decision_factors.factor: Presence and quality of a competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A competing offer from a company you would genuinely work for is the single most reliable lever for increasing any offer
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have an offer from a credible competitor at a comparable or higher total comp; never fabricate; evaluate your genuine willingness to accept it

decision_factors.factor: Province of employment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Pay transparency and salary history laws differ by province; BC has the Pay Transparency Act prohibiting salary history questions, Ontario does not have equivalent statutory protection
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify which province the role is in; in BC you can cite legal protection if salary history is asked; in Ontario, redirect tactfully without invoking law

decision_factors.factor: Round of negotiation
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether to use round anchor numbers or precise research-backed numbers
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track how many exchanges have occurred and how close both sides are to convergence

decision_factors.factor: Company retention posture
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether emergency retention budget exists and whether a market correction request will be taken seriously
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Is the company growing or in downsizing mode? Have you seen colleagues successfully negotiate off-cycle adjustments?

decision_factors.factor: Number of levers already exercised
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Once you've moved on base, equity, and signing bonus and the company has responded to all three, the negotiation space is exhausted
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count how many compensation components you've negotiated; if all three major levers are resolved, treat the package as final

decision_factors.factor: Timing of the ask relative to offer stage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Giving a number before an offer is made anchors you downward; negotiating only after receiving the written offer maximizes leverage
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track whether you are pre-offer, post-verbal-offer, or post-written-offer — each stage has a different appropriate script

decision_factors.factor: Geographic purchasing power differential
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Remote work from a lower-cost city dramatically increases effective compensation; a $200K role in NYC is equivalent to $280K+ in Austin in purchasing power
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use cost-of-living calculators to convert nominal comp to purchasing power equivalent across candidate's actual location vs. company's location

decision_factors.factor: Size of the signing bonus relative to financial reserves
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A large signing bonus with a cliff clawback creates meaningful financial risk if departure happens before the cliff; this risk scales with how much of the bonus you spend
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: if I had to repay the gross amount tomorrow, could I? If no, the bonus is not yet safe to spend.

decision_factors.factor: Whether the company has decided they want you before visa status is disclosed
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Leverage shifts dramatically once a company is invested in hiring you — sponsorship cost is weighed against losing a desired candidate, not against an unknown applicant
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Track whether you've received a verbal or written signal of intent to hire before any sponsorship conversation begins

decision_factors.factor: Which compensation dimensions have flexibility at this specific company
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Companies have asymmetric flexibility across comp components; salary may be locked by pay bands while signing bonuses, equity, and vacation are freely adjustable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: When salary hits resistance, ask 'What can you approve on your own?' to identify which levers remain open

decision_factors.factor: Total compensation versus base salary
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Two offers at the same base can differ by $100,000+ annually once equity, bonus, and signing bonus are included; comparing by base produces wrong rankings
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Build a full annual comp model: annualized equity (grant divided by vesting years), target bonus percentage, and base salary; treat signing bonus separately as non-recurring

decision_factors.factor: Whether employer has already invested in your work authorization
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prior LMIA investment by a current employer creates a sunk cost argument you can use in raise or retention discussions
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Determine whether your current employer paid LMIA fees and legal costs for you; if so, quantify the investment ($3,000–$6,000+) before the conversation

decision_factors.factor: Underlying reason for considering a move (in retention counter-offer scenarios)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If the reason for leaving is not purely financial, a counter-offer that only addresses money will not solve the problem
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself whether compensation was the primary driver or whether there are role, growth, or culture factors also at play

decision_factors.factor: Salary band constraints
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Even a willing manager may be structurally unable to approve above-band comp — understanding band limits sets realistic expectations
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR or your manager directly: 'What is the band for this role/level?' Some companies share this openly; others require indirect research

decision_factors.factor: Whether the candidate would actually leave for the BATNA
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Leverage that you would not actually use is not real leverage; the company may sense this and hold firm accordingly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself honestly: if this company doesn't move, will I actually take my alternative? If the answer is no, your stated leverage is weaker than it appears

decision_factors.factor: State-level salary history ban applicability
decision_factors.why_it_matters: In states with salary history bans, you have legal cover to refuse sharing current compensation, removing a key pressure tactic recruiters use
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Know whether your state has a salary history ban before any recruiter call; your deflection script differs depending on this

decision_factors.factor: Start date relative to review and bonus cycle
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Starting in October vs. November can affect bonus pro-ration and when your first performance review occurs, with material comp consequences
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask HR when the company's fiscal year, review cycle, and bonus cycle begin; map your proposed start date against those milestones

decision_factors.factor: Whether signing bonus is replacing unvested equity from a prior employer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: When a signing bonus is equity replacement, losing it via clawback means you lost both your prior equity AND the replacement — a double loss on a single departure
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Identify in the offer letter whether the signing bonus is explicitly described as equity compensation replacement. If yes, negotiating clawback protections becomes higher priority.

decision_factors.factor: Market compensation data for the role and level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Negotiating from objective market data removes the need to disclose personal need and establishes an external benchmark that is harder to dismiss than personal requests
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Use levels.fyi, H-1B salary disclosure data for the specific company and role, and peer data to establish a credible range before negotiating

decision_factors.factor: How differentiated your skills are relative to this company's core needs
decision_factors.why_it_matters: You are more valuable to companies where your specific skills are scarce and central; differentiation yields stronger offers and more negotiating room
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask 'What are the key projects defining this company's future, and how does someone get on those teams?' — assess fit between your strengths and their stated priorities

decision_factors.factor: Signing bonus recurrence and clawback terms
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Signing bonuses are one-time; modeling them as ongoing comp inflates perceived annual earnings; clawback provisions can require repayment if you leave early
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the signing bonus is subject to clawback and over what period; model annual comp without it

decision_factors.factor: Existence and quality of competing offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A real competing offer from an identifiable company is the single strongest negotiation lever regardless of immigration status
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether the competing offer is from a named company at a specific dollar amount — vague competing interest has far less force than a specific written offer

decision_factors.factor: Current tech salary growth market conditions
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Counter offer effectiveness remains high even as market conditions change, but baseline expectations should be calibrated accordingly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check current industry salary growth rates — as of 2025, tech salary growth has slowed to 1.6% vs. 3.5% in 2023

decision_factors.factor: Unvested equity and bonus proration impact of a transfer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An internal transfer may affect unvested equity vesting schedules or bonus eligibility, representing real hidden comp loss
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Review your equity grant schedule and bonus plan terms; ask HR explicitly how a transfer affects both

decision_factors.factor: Post-acceptance performance track record
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Post-acceptance negotiation only works if backed by demonstrated delivery; without it, the ask reads as entitlement rather than market correction
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have you delivered measurably beyond the original job scope, received strong feedback, or seen your responsibilities expand since joining?

decision_factors.factor: Whether non-cash levers are on the table
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Remote work arrangements, in-office day counts, and other non-cash terms have real life impact and are often more negotiable than base salary
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Scan the offer letter for what is unspecified — unspecified terms are open negotiation opportunities

decision_factors.factor: Whether PTO is guaranteed vs. accrual-based in year one
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Some companies require accrual before PTO can be used, which means you may not be able to use negotiated days until late in year one
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask explicitly: 'Is this an upfront PTO bank or does it accrue over time?' and get confirmation of first-year availability in writing

decision_factors.factor: Whether the student is negotiating from fear or from data
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Fear-based negotiation leads to accepting the first offer and systematically under-negotiating by 10–30% compared to domestic peers, compounding to hundreds of thousands of dollars over a career
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask yourself: is my counter grounded in a salary range from public data, or am I asking for what feels safe given my visa anxiety?

decision_factors.factor: How much the company has already invested in your interview process
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Sunk interview costs create strong pressure on the company to reach agreement; a company that has spent tens of thousands evaluating you is highly motivated not to lose you over modest salary differences
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count interview rounds completed, number of interviewers involved, time elapsed — more investment means more pressure on their side

decision_factors.factor: Fully diluted ownership percentage
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The percentage of the company your equity represents matters more than the raw number of shares; future dilution from funding rounds affects actual value
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask: 'What percentage of the company does this grant represent on a fully diluted basis?'; compare against 409A valuation to understand dollar value

decision_factors.factor: Quality of market comp data available
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Objective external anchors like levels.fyi or competing offers make negotiation concrete and harder to dismiss — without them, the negotiation is subjective
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Do you have recent, role-specific, level-specific data points with sample sizes? Single data points are weak; patterns across multiple sources are strong

decision_factors.factor: Deadline pressure on the offer
decision_factors.why_it_matters: An exploding offer compresses your ability to gather competing offers and make comparisons — extensions are almost always negotiable but require proactive action
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note the stated deadline and immediately assess whether you need more time; the sooner you request an extension, the more reasonable it appears

decision_factors.factor: Whether a title upgrade triggers equity re-grant at the higher level
decision_factors.why_it_matters: At some companies, a higher level code comes with equity grants calibrated to that level, making title negotiation a financial lever, not just a prestige lever
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask whether the level change comes with equity re-calibration; compare equity grant norms at the two levels using public compensation data

decision_factors.factor: Whether immigration commitment is confirmed in writing
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Verbal sponsorship promises are unenforceable; without written confirmation, the offer may be real on comp but not real on immigration
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Request explicit written confirmation of H-1B filing intent as part of the offer package before signing

decision_factors.factor: The long-term compounding effect of the current negotiation outcome
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each offer sets the baseline for future raises and the anchor for your next employer's offer; undercompensation compounds across decades
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate the 10-year gross value of a $5K salary difference; assess whether this role sets a comp baseline you want to carry forward

decision_factors.factor: Negotiation style: competitive firmness combined with collaborative warmth
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Research cited shows best negotiators combine firm outcome orientation with warm interpersonal approach; either alone is less effective
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your counter-offer framing expresses genuine enthusiasm for the role while being specific and firm about the compensation target

decision_factors.factor: Whether you've already revealed you're looking
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Revealing that you're job searching changes your relationship with your employer regardless of whether you stay — it signals flight risk and can affect future opportunities
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Have you told your manager, HR, or skip-level that you've been interviewing or received an offer?

decision_factors.factor: Pro dev budget accessibility and rollover
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A $5,000 pro dev budget is material for active upskilling, but only if it's accessible for your specific use case and doesn't expire unused
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask what the budget covers, who approves usage, and whether unused budget rolls over or is forfeited annually

decision_factors.factor: Whether justifications for requests are market-based vs. personal-need-based
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Market data ('comparable roles pay X') is far more persuasive than personal circumstance ('I have high rent'); the type of justification affects acceptance rate
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Before negotiating, gather external compensation benchmarks (Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Blind, peer offers) to anchor requests in market reality rather than personal need

decision_factors.factor: Candidate's visible enthusiasm and likelihood-to-sign signal
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Companies invest more negotiating effort in candidates they believe they can close; enthusiasm is itself a form of leverage when it signals genuine interest without desperation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether your communication throughout the process has conveyed excitement about the specific company and role, not just about compensation

decision_factors.factor: Work authorization framing clarity
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Canadian recruiters and hiring managers frequently misunderstand what PGWP means in practice — unclear framing causes rejection at the screening stage before qualifications are even evaluated
decision_factors.how_to_assess: If you are getting few or no callbacks despite strong qualifications, audit your resume and cover letter for any language that could imply employer sponsorship burden

decision_factors.factor: PGWP duration (tied to program length)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A 3-year PGWP gives significantly more runway for job search, 1 year of CEC-eligible experience accumulation, Express Entry submission, and PR approval than a 1-year PGWP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: PGWP duration equals your program length, capped at 3 years — a 2-year master's yields a 3-year PGWP; a 1-year post-grad certificate yields only a 1-year PGWP

decision_factors.factor: Company size and sponsorship infrastructure
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Large tech companies sponsor routinely with dedicated immigration teams; small startups often cannot or will not sponsor unless the candidate is irreplaceable
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check job postings for explicit sponsorship language; ask recruiter directly; use community databases (e.g., H-1B employer data from USCIS public filings)

decision_factors.factor: Point of contact: hiring manager vs. HR vs. recruiter
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Managers engage to solve a business problem and can override HR friction; HR screens against checklists including sponsorship flags, making them a much lower-yield contact for international candidates
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Search LinkedIn for the team lead, engineering manager, or director over the relevant function; avoid titles like 'Recruiter,' 'Talent Acquisition,' or 'HR'

decision_factors.factor: Advisor's industry internship pipeline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For industry-track PhDs, the advisor's ability to place students in internships at top AI labs and tech companies is the primary lever for post-PhD job outcomes — more impactful than program rank
decision_factors.how_to_assess: During PhD visits, ask where their last 5 students interned and where they ended up; verify independently via LinkedIn

decision_factors.factor: Remaining OPT time before next H-1B cap season deadline
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines urgency and which options are still viable — if less than one cap cycle remains, some paths (like finding a new sponsor) may be technically possible but extremely time-compressed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count months remaining on STEM OPT, confirm when H-1B registration opens (typically early March), and determine whether you have enough runway to find a job, negotiate an offer, and get written sponsorship commitment before registration

decision_factors.factor: Equity instrument type: RSU vs. NSO vs. ISO
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Each type has a fundamentally different tax treatment and risk profile — RSU taxes as ordinary income at vest, NSO taxes as ordinary income at exercise, ISO can trigger AMT
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the offer letter or equity agreement for the explicit label (RSU, NSO, ISO); do not assume — ask HR or legal

decision_factors.factor: Whether HR raises salary at the very start of the process
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Early salary discussion signals low flexibility — the role has a fixed band with little or no negotiation room, and HR is using it as a filter criterion rather than a negotiation starting point
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Note at what stage HR first brings up compensation. If it's in the initial phone screen, the band is likely rigid.

decision_factors.factor: Industry growth trajectory

decision_factors.factor: Vesting schedule structure (uniform vs. back-weighted)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A back-weighted schedule (e.g., Snapchat 10/20/30/40) means an employee who leaves at year 2 captures only 30% of total grant value, while a uniform schedule (25% per year) would yield 50% — a massive difference in realized compensation
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Read the offer letter carefully for the vest percentage per year; if not specified, ask HR directly. Compare to standard 4-year/1-year-cliff model

decision_factors.factor: Candidate-to-role match percentage

decision_factors.factor: Canadian local network presence

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency (TEF/TCF scores)

decision_factors.factor: Which visa stage you are currently in (OPT vs. STEM OPT vs. needing H-1B)

decision_factors.factor: Visa status disclosure timing

decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess whether you have had at least one real conversation where the manager has expressed genuine interest; if yes, the timing is right to raise it

decision_factors.factor: Target role type within 'industry research'

decision_factors.factor: Company stage: public vs. pre-IPO startup
