failure_patterns.pattern: Refusing to state a salary expectation and asking HR to make the first offer
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates have absorbed the negotiation advice 'never reveal your bottom line first' and apply it in a context where it actively backfires — the HR-candidate dynamic is not a symmetric negotiation
failure_patterns.consequence: HR is put in an impossible position; they cannot finalize a number without candidate input, so the process stalls or HR makes a low internal recommendation to hedge the uncertainty
warning_signs: Candidate says 'whatever your standard is, just tell me'
Candidate says 'I have no salary requirements, I care more about the platform'
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Comparing offers by raw score totals without applying personal importance weights
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Weighted scoring requires self-knowledge about values; raw totals feel more objective and require less introspection
failure_patterns.consequence: Choosing the wrong offer — the case example shows raw scores favoring Offer A (390 vs 370) while weighted scores strongly favor Offer B (104 vs 69)
warning_signs: Saying 'Offer A scored higher overall so I'll pick it'
Treating all factors as equally important without explicitly assigning weights
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting a below-market offer expecting performance to close the gap over time
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Recruiter or manager reassures the candidate that good work will be rewarded with raises comparable to peers — candidate takes this at face value and deprioritizes negotiation at offer stage
failure_patterns.consequence: Because raises are applied as a percentage of base, a lower starting salary creates a permanent compounding disadvantage; the candidate never reaches parity with peers who started higher
warning_signs: Recruiter says 'prove yourself first and we'll make it right'
Candidate thinks 'I'll negotiate after I show my value in the role'

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting the offer and planning to renegotiate after a successful probation period
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates feel grateful or anxious about losing the offer; they rationalize that proving themselves first will make the ask easier and safer
failure_patterns.consequence: The labor contract locks in the salary; HR has no budget or process mechanism to adjust outside review cycles; the informal promise from the recruiter is unenforceable
warning_signs: Candidate says 'I'll just show them what I can do first'
Recruiter makes a vague verbal promise about 'adjusting after probation' instead of putting it in the offer letter
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Evaluating an offer based only on base salary without modeling annualized equity value
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Base salary is the most salient, immediately legible number; equity vesting schedules require multi-step calculation that most first-time job seekers haven't been taught
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidates accept lower total compensation packages or negotiate the wrong component, leaving significant money on the table
warning_signs: Candidate asks only 'what is the base salary?' and stops there
Candidate compares offers by base salary alone without building a year-by-year compensation model
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Giving a vague salary range instead of a specific number
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates fear commitment and hope flexibility will help them; they anchor low with the floor of their range without realizing it
failure_patterns.consequence: Recruiter anchors to the low end of the range; candidate feels underpaid but has no grounds to push back since they gave the number
warning_signs: Saying '5k–10k is fine'
Saying 'somewhere around X to Y'
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Spending weeks on cold applications to large tech companies before switching to networking
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Large company brand names feel like high-value targets; cold application is low effort per application so it feels productive; candidates underestimate how flooded these pipelines are
failure_patterns.consequence: Wasted 4+ weeks with minimal traction (2 phone screens from 80+ applications); timeline pressure increases as PGWP expiration approaches
warning_signs: Applying to Amazon, Google, Shopify Canada exclusively in early weeks
Using LinkedIn Easy Apply for roles showing 500+ applicants

failure_patterns.pattern: Delaying IELTS/language test preparation until after starting the job search
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates focus on immediate job search activity and deprioritize language testing, not realizing CRS score optimization requires scores submitted before Express Entry pool entry
failure_patterns.consequence: Weak language scores suppress CRS score at the point of profile submission, reducing ITA probability during the window of eligibility
warning_signs: Starting Express Entry profile without English test scores finalized
Having no French test score when French proficiency could realistically be achieved

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating 'will you require sponsorship in the future' as equivalent to 'are you authorized to work now'
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates conflate current authorization with future sponsorship need, leading to inaccurate answers that either overstate or understate their situation
failure_patterns.consequence: Answering 'yes' to future sponsorship for OPT-only situations may filter out candidates unnecessarily; answering 'no' when H-1B will be needed creates legal and trust issues
warning_signs: Candidate says they 'need sponsorship' when on OPT
Candidate says they will 'never' need sponsorship without acknowledging future H-1B need

failure_patterns.pattern: Opening the cold email with visa sponsorship needs
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: International students are conditioned to be upfront about constraints and feel that disclosing sponsorship requirements early is honest and efficient
failure_patterns.consequence: Triggers a sponsorship rejection filter before the hiring manager reads the candidate's qualifications; the candidate never gets a chance to demonstrate value
warning_signs: First or second sentence of the email mentions OPT, PGWP, H-1B, or sponsorship
Email subject line includes 'international student' or 'work authorization'

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating 'industry research' as a single homogeneous career target rather than a spectrum
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The label 'Research Scientist' or 'Applied Scientist' sounds uniform, but the actual role requirements, publication expectations, and PhD prerequisites vary enormously across companies and teams
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidates prepare for and evaluate programs against the wrong criteria for their actual target role, leading to misaligned advisor choices, publication strategies, and internship targeting
warning_signs: Using 'industry research' without specifying the target company tier or role type
Assuming all research scientist roles require the same PhD profile

failure_patterns.pattern: Assuming a reputable or large company will reliably follow through on immigration commitments
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Brand trust heuristic — large, well-known employers feel stable and trustworthy, leading candidates to skip verification steps they would apply to smaller firms
failure_patterns.consequence: Company policy changes (layoffs, budget cuts, legal risk assessments) can eliminate sponsorship programs regardless of company size, leaving employees without recourse
warning_signs: Candidate says 'they're a big company, I'm not worried'
No written sponsorship language requested because the company 'has a known sponsorship history'

failure_patterns.pattern: Early exercising ISO options without understanding AMT exposure
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Employees are told early exercise is a tax optimization strategy (start the capital gains clock early); they act without modeling the AMT liability under different stock price scenarios
failure_patterns.consequence: If the stock price drops post-exercise, the employee holds worthless or low-value stock but still owes AMT calculated on the original paper gain — the mechanism behind thousands of 2000-era bankruptcies
warning_signs: Employee exercises ISO options at a paper gain but does not immediately sell shares
Employee does not consult a tax professional before exercising
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Fabricating or inflating current salary figures
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates believe HR has no way to verify the number and use it to create a higher anchor for negotiation
failure_patterns.consequence: Background checks, bank statement requests, and payslip verification expose the lie — offer is rescinded at the final stage, which is a complete waste of both parties' time
warning_signs: Candidate hesitates or gives vague answers when asked for salary breakdown details
Stated salary is unusually high relative to experience level and market data
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Counting unvested equity and promised raises as real compensation in offer comparisons
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Recruiters present total comp including equity and raise projections, making it feel like guaranteed income; anchoring bias inflates its perceived value
failure_patterns.consequence: Overestimating one offer's value and making a suboptimal choice based on compensation that may never materialize
warning_signs: Including '4-year vesting schedule' totals in your offer comparison spreadsheet
Factoring in 'up to X% annual raise' language in the offer letter
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Raising compensation concerns only after onboarding, once fully committed
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The candidate felt the offer stage was too early or too risky to push back; they hoped their dissatisfaction would fade
failure_patterns.consequence: No leverage remains — switching costs (housing, visa, social insurance timelines) make leaving expensive; the company has little incentive to re-negotiate a signed contract
warning_signs: Candidate says 'I'll bring it up once I've proven myself'
Candidate mutters dissatisfaction but signs without saying anything
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Forfeiting vested options at departure because the 90-day exercise window is not planned for
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Employees focus on the new job excitement and don't calculate the cash needed to exercise options until it's too late; the 90-day clock starts immediately at termination
failure_patterns.consequence: Potentially tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in vested compensation permanently forfeited
warning_signs: Employee is leaving a company without having checked the post-termination exercise period
Employee has not calculated the cash required to exercise all vested options
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Failing to document all components of current compensation before negotiating
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates know their monthly take-home intuitively but have never summed the full package; they assume the recruiter will ask follow-up questions
failure_patterns.consequence: Post-offer renegotiation attempts look dishonest and damage trust; the recruiter may move to the second-choice candidate rather than re-open the approval process
warning_signs: Can only quote monthly base when asked about compensation
Has never computed annual total comp including bonuses and benefits
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Not asking what 'no sponsorship' means before self-eliminating
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Fear of rejection causes candidates to accept the phrase at face value rather than probe for specifics
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidates miss roles they are fully eligible for — particularly STEM OPT extension-eligible candidates whose additional authorization is compatible with company policy
warning_signs: Candidate stops applying after seeing 'no sponsorship' in a posting
Candidate doesn't ask follow-up questions when recruiter says 'we don't sponsor'

failure_patterns.pattern: Sending cold emails to HR or recruiter inboxes instead of hiring managers
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: HR and recruiter contacts are the most publicly listed and feel like the 'official' channel; candidates mistake official for effective
failure_patterns.consequence: Application enters the same screening funnel as job board submissions, with the same sponsorship filters and low callback rates
warning_signs: Contact's LinkedIn title includes 'Recruiter,' 'Talent Acquisition,' or 'HR'
Candidate is using the company's careers page contact email rather than a specific person's address

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating equity grants as certain income when a company has not yet IPO'd or been acquired
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The nominal dollar value in the offer letter feels real; candidates anchor to it and factor it into lifestyle decisions
failure_patterns.consequence: If the company fails to IPO or be acquired, RSU and options are worth zero — employees who made financial decisions based on expected equity value suffer significant losses
warning_signs: Candidate says 'I'm getting $500K in RSU' about a pre-IPO company as if it is cash
Candidate declines a public company offer in favor of a startup primarily because of the stated RSU value
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Conflating the recruiter's question about salary expectation with the final offer
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates don't understand that when HR asks for expected salary early in the process, it is often intelligence gathering — not a binding negotiation — and panic-anchor to a low number
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate inadvertently sets a low ceiling before the hiring team has fully evaluated them, leaving money on the table
warning_signs: Candidate quotes a number in early phone screen without being asked to negotiate
Candidate lowers their expectation preemptively 'to seem reasonable'
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Making offer decisions without first clarifying your core priority
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: People feel pressure to decide quickly and skip the introspective step; or they assume their priority is obvious (money) without testing whether it's actually consistent with their constraints
failure_patterns.consequence: Applying inconsistent weights across factors, feeling regret after choosing, or choosing based on others' frameworks rather than your own situation
warning_signs: Asking 'which offer is better?' without specifying your own situation or goals
Borrowing someone else's scoring framework verbatim without adjusting weights
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Negotiating with no market data and no competing offer — just a vague sense that 'I deserve more'
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidate knows negotiation is allowed but has not done the preparation to make a credible case
failure_patterns.consequence: HR has nothing to take back to leadership; the ask sounds arbitrary and is easily dismissed; candidate may still accept the same offer, having gained nothing
warning_signs: Candidate says 'I just feel the number is low' without citing comparables
No other offer or current salary benchmark to reference
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Not asking new employer to cover option exercise costs as part of sign-on negotiation
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates don't know this is a negotiable item; they assume sign-on bonus is a fixed goodwill gesture, not a tool to compensate for leaving money behind
failure_patterns.consequence: Employee either forfeits vested options (loss of asset) or funds the exercise personally (cash strain) when the new employer could have covered it
warning_signs: Candidate mentions they have unvested equity or options costs but doesn't raise it with new employer
Candidate accepts sign-on bonus without disclosing what they are leaving behind at current company
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Accepting HR's framing that 'maximum raise is X%' as a fixed constraint
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The policy sounds official and candidates feel they have no standing to challenge a stated company rule
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate leaves money on the table; the real ceiling (with special approval) was higher, but candidate never triggered the escalation process
warning_signs: Immediately accepting the first number after HR mentions a policy
Not asking whether exceptions or special approvals exist
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Sending long, dense cold emails (over 150 words)
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates feel they need to establish full credibility in the first email; more information feels safer and more thorough
failure_patterns.consequence: Email is skimmed or ignored; the volume of content signals a lack of awareness of the recipient's time constraints
warning_signs: Email includes full work history summary
Email explains the candidate's entire project in detail before any relationship exists

failure_patterns.pattern: Applying generic negotiation tactics (e.g., 'never show your cards') without understanding the HR-candidate structural dynamic
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Advice from negotiation books or online posts is context-free and does not account for the fact that HR must mediate between candidate and hiring team — they need candidate input to advocate effectively
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate comes across as evasive or strategically naive; HR cannot build a case internally, reducing the chance of getting the full salary authorized
warning_signs: Candidate reflexively deflects every salary question
Candidate treats the HR interview as adversarial rather than collaborative
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Underweighting or ignoring the direct manager when evaluating offers
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Manager quality is hard to assess before joining; candidates focus on observable/quantifiable factors like salary and company brand
failure_patterns.consequence: Ending up with a technically good offer at a good company but miserable daily experience due to an incompatible or poor manager
warning_signs: Not asking about reporting structure during interviews
Not researching the direct manager's background or management style
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Ignoring equity refresh when evaluating long-term compensation trajectory at a company
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Equity refresh is almost never mentioned in the offer letter; candidates assume the original grant represents the steady-state compensation indefinitely
failure_patterns.consequence: Employee reaches year 3-4 with declining forward compensation and no leverage to negotiate internally, or is blindsided when their total comp drops
warning_signs: Candidate can state their initial RSU grant but cannot describe the refresh policy
Candidate has been at a company 2+ years and has never received an equity refresh discussion in performance review
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Treating future equity, bonuses, and growth opportunities as equivalent to current base salary in negotiations
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: HR actively promotes these as substitutes; candidates are susceptible to optimistic narratives, especially at growing companies
failure_patterns.consequence: Candidate accepts a lower base on the strength of uncertain future payouts that may never arrive; they are locked into the lower base for all future raise calculations
warning_signs: Feeling satisfied after recruiter mentions 'great stock options'
Mentally adding unconfirmed bonus to base to reach a target number
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Negotiating without a competing offer or any leverage when market conditions are weak
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates feel pressure to close quickly in a tough job market and overestimate their negotiating position
failure_patterns.consequence: Pushing too hard without leverage leads to offer rescission or the recruiter turning to other candidates; candidate ends up with nothing
warning_signs: Only one active application
Long job search with no other offers pending
Candidate has told the recruiter they have no other options
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

failure_patterns.pattern: Inflating or fabricating salary history to anchor the negotiation higher
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Candidates believe they can get away with unverifiable claims; they want to establish a higher baseline
failure_patterns.consequence: Employers increasingly cross-check via bank statements, tax records, and background checks; fabrication can result in offer rescission, contract termination, and industry blacklisting
warning_signs: Candidate is slow or evasive when asked for salary proof
Stated salary is inconsistent across documents
failure_patterns._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the job posting located in British Columbia, Ontario, PEI, or another Canadian province?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which provincial pay transparency statute, if any, applies to the posting
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If BC, Ontario (25+ employees), or PEI (10+ employees): confirm whether the employer meets the size threshold and whether the effective date has passed; expect or require a posted salary range
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Alberta, Quebec, or another province without enacted legislation: no pay transparency posting obligation applies; candidate cannot rely on a posted range

diagnostic_questions.question: What SOC code does the employer intend to use on the LCA for this position?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which OEWS wage table and thresholds apply; different SOC codes for the same job title can produce wage differences of $30,000–$90,000+ at the same level and MSA
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Verify the SOC code accurately reflects the primary job duties; look up the prevailing wage for that SOC at the applicable MSA and level via FLC Data Center
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: SOC code is required for LCA filing; employer must select one before proceeding

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the BC employer have 1,000 or more employees, 300–999, 50–299, or fewer than 50 employees?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which phase-in date applies for BC pay transparency posting obligations under Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Identify the corresponding required start date: 1,000+ from Nov 1, 2023; 300–999 from Jan 1, 2024; 50–299 from Jan 1, 2025; all employers from Jan 1, 2026
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If fewer than 50 employees and before January 1, 2026: not yet required to post salary ranges; after January 1, 2026 the 'all employers' rule applies

diagnostic_questions.question: Which wage level (I–IV) is the employer assigning to this H-1B position?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines the minimum prevailing wage floor AND, effective February 27, 2026, the number of H-1B lottery entries (1–4) the petition will receive
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Compare the assigned level against DOL complexity criteria; assess whether actual job duties support a higher level classification
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Wage level must be assigned before LCA filing; it must reflect actual job duties, not the employer's preferred salary range

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Ontario employer have 25 or more employees?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the Ontario employer is covered by the Working for Workers Four Act, 2024, S.O. 2024, c. 15, Schedule 2 salary range disclosure requirement
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Employer must include compensation range or fixed salary in job postings effective January 1, 2026
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Employer is not covered by Ontario's pay transparency posting requirement; candidate cannot legally require a posted range

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the employer previously filed H-1B LCAs for comparable roles in the same occupation and MSA?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Prior OFLC performance data filings reveal the employer's actual disclosed wage history, which may exceed the OEWS minimum floor and establishes a data-backed negotiation benchmark
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Search OFLC Performance Data at DOL website for the employer's prior filings; use disclosed wages as a negotiation data point
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Rely on OEWS prevailing wage from FLC Data Center as the minimum floor benchmark

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the role being hired in British Columbia — meaning, is the salary history ban legally in effect for this hiring process?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the employer is legally prohibited from asking about pay history and using it to set wages
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate is legally protected from salary history questions; employer cannot ask at any point in the hiring process under Pay Transparency Act, SBC 2023, Chapter 18
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Ontario or other province without a salary history ban: employer may legally ask about prior pay; candidate must decide how to respond without legal protection

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the worker a national of India or China in the EB-2 PERM backlog?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Tests whether PERM-based green card sponsorship is a practical path, given the multi-decade visa backlog for Indian and Chinese EB-2 nationals and the dual-date wage compliance requirement
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Note that the visa wait for Indian EB-2 nationals is estimated at 134+ years; wage compliance must hold at the time of actual visa receipt, making PERM a theoretical rather than actionable path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: PERM may be a viable green card path; confirm prevailing wage compliance requirements apply at both filing and visa issuance dates

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the BC employer above the annual pay transparency report threshold (1,000+, 300–999, or 50–299 employees) and has the relevant reporting date passed?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the employer has filed a publicly accessible annual pay transparency report that a candidate could review to infer internal pay equity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate may be able to locate the employer's annual pay transparency report to inform negotiation strategy regarding internal pay equity
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Annual reporting obligation has not yet applied to this employer; report may not be available

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the H-1B petition cap-subject and filed on or after February 27, 2026?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the wage-weighted lottery rule (Federal Register 2025-23853) applies, which ties the number of lottery entries directly to the wage level assigned
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: The wage level assigned has direct lottery probability consequences; Level IV receives 4 entries vs. 1 for Level I — salary negotiation that changes the wage level also changes selection probability
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Prior lottery rules apply; wage level affects only the minimum compensation floor, not lottery entry count

diagnostic_questions.question: What wage level (I, II, III, or IV) will the employer file the LCA at for this role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines the candidate's baseline lottery entry count and whether there is an actionable path to negotiate up to a higher level
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Level III or IV: how close is the offered salary to the Level IV threshold? Is there room to negotiate further?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Level I or II: what is the exact salary threshold to reach Level III for this SOC code and location, and is the gap closeable through negotiation?

diagnostic_questions.question: What state do you physically live and work in — and is it different from the employer's headquarters?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which state's salary history ban law applies and whether the candidate has legal protection they may not know about
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Your state's law likely applies to you regardless of employer HQ — check whether your state has an active ban before your next interview
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Check whether your state has a ban; if not, check for applicable municipal ordinances in your city

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you comparing this offer to Canadian market data or US market data?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's reference point is calibrated to the Canadian market or will systematically mislead their negotiation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Which Canadian sources are you using — Robert Half Canada, Glassdoor CA, or something else?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You need to recalibrate entirely — US benchmarks are 25–40% higher and will cause you to either lose the offer or leave money on the table

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this a new cap-subject H-1B filing, a transfer, or a renewal of an existing approved H-1B?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the weighted lottery rule applies at all — existing approved H-1B holders are not subject to re-selection and have different negotiation leverage
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If new cap-subject filing: wage level is critical for lottery odds — prioritize wage level threshold analysis
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If existing approved H-1B: the retention/lottery-risk-avoidance argument is the primary lever — focus on replacement cost framing

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you already disclosed your current or past salary at any point in this process?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the anchor has already been set and what recovery strategy is available
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Was it voluntary or in response to a direct question? If you're in a ban state and they asked, you may have documentation leverage. Either way, reframe forward immediately.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You have full negotiating flexibility — do not disclose before an offer is made

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this offer from a FAANG Canada employer (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Shopify) or a mid-tier / enterprise Canadian company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether to benchmark against FAANG Canada ranges (20–40% above Robert Half) or against the broad Robert Half / Glassdoor CA market ranges
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are you negotiating RSU grants and vesting schedule, or only base salary?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Focus on signing bonus as the primary negotiating lever since base bands tend to be narrower and more fixed

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the candidate know the DOL prevailing wage for their specific SOC code and metro area, and the salary breakpoints between wage levels?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the candidate can make a structurally grounded wage-level argument, or is relying only on market comp data which is insufficient for H-1B negotiation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: verify that the duties of the role actually support the higher wage level classification, not just the salary
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: candidate needs to research DOL OEWS data or consult with an immigration attorney before entering salary negotiation

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the company post a salary range in the job listing, or are they required to by law in your state?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Reveals whether you already have the employer's budget information, which fundamentally changes your negotiation opening
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Use the posted range as your anchor; open by targeting the upper end with explicit justification
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You'll need to research market data from other sources (levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Blind, Bureau of Labor Statistics) to establish your target range independently

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the offer include RSUs or stock options, and do you know the 4-year vesting value?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands their actual total compensation or is only evaluating base salary
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you compared the RSU grant size to benchmarks for your level at this company?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Request the full equity breakdown immediately — at senior levels RSUs can represent 30–50% of total comp and are negotiable

diagnostic_questions.question: How much has the employer already invested in this candidate's immigration process (fees, attorney time, prior filings)?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Quantifies the employer's sunk cost and the incremental risk they face from turnover under the new lottery system, which calibrates how strong the retention argument is
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If significant investment: the retention premium argument is strong — frame replacement cost explicitly including lottery re-entry risk
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If early stage with no prior investment: retention argument is weaker; focus on wage level threshold and market comp arguments instead

diagnostic_questions.question: Was the salary history question asked in writing (application form, email) or verbally in an interview?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines how easy it is to document the violation and the strength of evidence if you choose to escalate
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Screenshot or save the written request immediately — written evidence substantially strengthens any complaint or legal action
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Document immediately after the interview: date, interviewer name, exact wording recalled, any witnesses present

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the role in Alberta (Calgary/Edmonton) or in Ontario/BC?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate needs to apply an 8–12% take-home premium to Alberta gross salary before comparing to Ontario/BC offers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you calculated the after-tax take-home difference, not just gross salary comparison?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you aware that Ontario and BC provincial income taxes will reduce take-home by 8–12% more than an equivalent Alberta salary?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the candidate aware that wage level is determined by job duties (SOC code) rather than salary alone?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Identifies whether the candidate risks negotiating a salary increase that looks like a wage level upgrade but isn't, due to misunderstanding how the DOL classification works
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If yes: confirm they have verified with immigration counsel that the duties support the higher level classification before using it as a negotiation anchor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If no: candidate must understand this before negotiating — a higher salary without matching duties classification yields no additional lottery entries

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this an internal promotion or an external new hire situation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Some states' salary history bans only cover external hires, not internal compensation changes — this changes what protections apply
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Check whether your state extends the ban to internal promotions (Washington does explicitly; most others may not)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Standard salary history ban protections for new hires apply if you're in a ban state

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you asked about the signing bonus yet?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has left the most immediately negotiable component of a Canadian tech offer unclaimed
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What number did you ask for, and what was the response?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask before you accept — signing bonuses are expected to be requested at Canadian tech companies even when base is fixed

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you an international candidate comparing a Canadian offer to a US offer, and what is your immigration pathway in each country?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is factoring in immigration stability premium (Canadian PR in 1–2 years vs. H-1B uncertainty + potential 134-year green card wait) into the compensation comparison
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: How are you weighting immigration security vs. the compensation gap — especially at FAANG level where the US gap is severe?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Even if both offers are from Canadian employers, understanding your PR timeline affects how much negotiating risk you can afford to take

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your years of experience, and what level/title is the role being offered?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is being correctly leveled — mis-leveling down costs $25K–$40K annually in Canada
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the offered base salary align with Robert Half Canada ranges for that experience tier in your city?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Map your YOE to the junior/mid/senior bands and verify the offer falls within the correct range before negotiating the number

diagnostic_questions.question: What specific type of work permit do you currently hold — is it open or employer-specific?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines the actual level of negotiation leverage available; this is the single most important variable before any other advice is relevant
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If open (PGWP): What is your PGWP expiry date, and have you calculated whether you can achieve PR before that date?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If employer-specific: Who is the employer named on the permit, and have you identified any GTS-approved alternative employers you could approach for competing offers?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a competing offer with a specific number?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have BATNA leverage that changes the entire counter structure
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is the competing offer from a company you would genuinely consider joining? If yes, use that number as your direct anchor rather than a 10–20% counter above the initial offer.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you in a position to generate a competing offer before the deadline? If not, proceed with market data as your anchor.

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a real, written external offer with a specific number and deadline?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have actual leverage in the internal negotiation or are negotiating from comfort
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Are you genuinely willing to take the external offer if the company doesn't match? If not, your leverage is partially a bluff
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Is obtaining an external offer feasible before your internal negotiation window? If not, shift strategy to market data and business case framing

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a specific number below which you will walk away from this offer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has a real BATNA or is negotiating without an anchor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is that number based on a real alternative — current comp, competing offer — or an arbitrary preference?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Stop negotiating until you identify your walk-away number; without it you cannot negotiate effectively

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a competing offer, and if so, what is the exact number and deadline?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have external leverage to use — a competing offer fundamentally changes the negotiation dynamic and the scripts available to you
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is it from a company the hiring company would consider a credible competitor, and are you willing to name it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: What market data do you have from sources like levels.fyi that can serve as a proxy for external validation?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the remote work arrangement stated explicitly in the offer letter, or only communicated verbally?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has actually secured flexible work terms or is operating on an informal understanding that has no enforcement mechanism
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does it say 'fully remote' specifically, or use softer language like 'remote-friendly' or 'we prefer remote'?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Why haven't you asked for it in writing, and what is your plan if the arrangement changes after you join?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the clawback clause specify that it applies 'for any reason or no reason,' or does it limit triggers to voluntary resignation and termination for cause?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the employee bears clawback risk even for layoffs — a distinction that determines if the clause is standard-protective or adversarially written
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: The clause is high-risk. Is there still time to negotiate exclusion language before signing? If not, treat the bonus as fully contingent for the entire period.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Confirm that 'termination without cause' and 'reduction in force' are explicitly named as exclusions — absence of the 'any reason' phrase alone is not sufficient protection

diagnostic_questions.question: Has this company sponsored H-1B before, and what is their historical approval rate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the offer is executable on immigration — a company with no prior H-1B history or low approval rates is a fundamentally different risk than one with a track record
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Who is their immigration counsel, and can you get written confirmation of sponsorship intent in the offer?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do they have immigration counsel retained? Are they willing to commit in writing? If neither, treat the immigration component of the offer as unconfirmed.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you received a formal or informal signal that the company wants to hire you — or are you still in evaluation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you are in 'Yes-If' (post-hiring-decision) or 'No-But' (still being evaluated) status, which determines how much leverage you actually have
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What specific comp dimensions have they discussed — salary only, or total package including bonus and equity?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Defer all compensation discussion until you receive an offer signal; negotiating during evaluation forces premature compromise

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you calculated the full annual total compensation for each offer, including annualized equity, target bonus, and base — excluding the signing bonus?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is comparing offers on a valid apples-to-apples basis or defaulting to base salary comparison
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: What is the annualized equity value and what discount rate did you apply based on company stage?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The offer ranking may be reversed once full comp is modeled; what is the equity grant, vesting schedule, and bonus target for each offer?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you accumulated 12 months of NOC TEER 0/1 Canadian work experience?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether you are currently eligible to apply for CEC Express Entry, which is the mechanism for eliminating LMIA dependency
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you created an Express Entry profile and received an ITA? If not, this is the most urgent action to restore or preserve negotiation leverage.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How many months remain until you reach 12 months, and does that timeline fit within your PGWP validity with sufficient buffer for PR processing?

diagnostic_questions.question: How does the initial offer compare to the levels.fyi median for this specific company, level, and location?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: How aggressive your counter should be — a below-market offer justifies a 20–25% counter vs. 10–12% for a market-rate offer
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the offer is more than 15% below median, prepare specific data points to justify the larger counter.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the offer is at or above median, a 10–12% counter is appropriate and a larger counter may face pushback without stronger justification.

diagnostic_questions.question: If your current job paid exactly what you're asking for, would you still want to stay?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the dissatisfaction is purely compensation or driven by scope, manager, team, or career ceiling
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Then a retention counter-offer addresses the root cause — evaluate whether the comp offered is competitive
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Then money alone won't fix the problem — a retention counter-offer buys time but not satisfaction; evaluate the external offer on its full merits

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a competing offer, and would you genuinely consider taking it?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The actual strength of your leverage; a competing offer you wouldn't take is weak leverage
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Share the number with the target company; you don't have to name the employer
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Assess whether you have time to generate one before your decision deadline

diagnostic_questions.question: At what stage are you — pre-offer, post-verbal-offer, or post-written-offer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which phase of negotiation strategy applies — deflection scripts, time-buying scripts, or active counter scripts are each stage-specific
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If post-written-offer: have you identified every unspecified term in the letter that could be negotiated?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If pre-offer: are you being asked for salary expectations, and do you know whether your state has a salary history ban?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you know which budget your target lever (remote, PTO, pro dev, signing bonus) comes from — salary/HR or the hiring manager's discretionary budget?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands who actually has the authority to approve the ask, which determines how to route the request
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you framed your ask to the right decision-maker, or are you going through HR for something the hiring manager could approve directly?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You may be negotiating with the wrong person; ask the recruiter who owns approval for each specific lever before making the ask

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the clawback structured as a cliff or as prorated repayment?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: How much financial risk you carry at any point during the clawback period. Cliff structures mean maximum liability for the entire period; prorated structures reduce exposure over time.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If prorated: confirm the formula — how is remaining obligation calculated? Monthly? By exact day?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If cliff: negotiate prorated before signing. If not possible, do not spend the signing bonus until the cliff clears.

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your OPT end date, and when is the next H-1B cap filing window?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: How much time pressure you're actually under — which determines whether you have runway to run a multi-company search or whether you're in a deadline-driven single-offer scenario
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you have 6+ months, you have time for parallel processes; treat this like any other negotiation with competing offers as the goal.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you're within 90 days of OPT expiration, identify your real BATNA — STEM OPT extension, another degree, CPT, or another country's job market — before entering any negotiation.

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have any competing offers, or imminent offers from companies you would actually work for?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have real market leverage or are negotiating purely on assertion; competing offers are the most powerful single source of negotiating power
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Do the offer windows actually overlap — is the competing offer still active right now?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you actively interviewing elsewhere, and can you compress timelines to create overlap? If not, your leverage must come from other sources — quantified value propositions, market data, or demonstrated alternatives

diagnostic_questions.question: What stage is the company — public, pre-IPO Series C/D, or early-stage Seed/A?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Which equity valuation framework applies and how much weight to give the equity component in financial planning
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: For pre-IPO: have you asked for the 409A valuation and the liquidation preference structure?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If company stage is unknown, the candidate cannot accurately value the equity or assess liquidity risk

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the employer you are negotiating with (or any competing employer you are considering) appear on the Global Talent Stream designation list?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether competing offers are practically usable as leverage (GTS = ~2 weeks) or theoretically usable but practically slow (standard LMIA = 2–5 months)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: GTS-approved competing employers give you real walk-away power even without open work authorization; use competing offer leverage normally.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The competing offer may not be credible as a lever if the LMIA timeline makes it impractical; assess whether to disclose it or seek a GTS-approved alternative first

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the offer exploding — do you have a hard deadline, and how much time do you have?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have time to generate competing offers or whether you must negotiate from your current position
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Prioritize negotiating the current offer aggressively since you cannot create additional leverage in the available time.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Consider whether generating a competing offer before engaging in negotiation would strengthen your position.

diagnostic_questions.question: How many months into your current promotion cycle are you?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The true hidden cost of accepting an internal transfer at the same level — the more time elapsed, the more a clock reset costs you
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 6+ months in, calculate: months elapsed + new promo clock length to understand total delay before negotiating transfer terms
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If early in cycle, the promo clock impact is smaller but still worth quantifying and negotiating compensation for

diagnostic_questions.question: How many rounds have you already completed, and which levers have you moved?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Where you are in the negotiation arc and how much room remains
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you've addressed base, equity, and signing bonus across two or more rounds, you may be at or near the ceiling
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you've only pushed on base, shift to other levers before concluding there's no room

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the negotiation happening by phone or email?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have real-time advocacy from the recruiter or whether you're getting batched, low-friction responses
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If phone: have you prepared your specific number and practiced the silence after delivering it?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If email: have you requested a 15-minute call before submitting any counter?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the signing bonus have a clawback provision, and if so, what is the repayment window and does it prorate?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The true financial risk of the signing bonus relative to how long you expect to stay and how certain you are about the role
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is the clawback full repayment or prorated? How does that affect your break-even tenure?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You need to read the offer letter or bonus agreement carefully before signing — this is almost always present and is a material financial obligation

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the repayment obligation specify gross amount or net-of-taxes amount?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you could realistically repay the clawback from what you actually received, or whether you'd face a shortfall
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If gross: calculate the actual repayment gap (bonus x effective tax rate) and decide if this is acceptable risk. Try to negotiate net language.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If net or silent: get explicit written confirmation that repayment is net-based — verbal assurance is insufficient

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your real BATNA — what would you actually do if this offer fell through?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your negotiating leverage is genuine or performed — a BATNA only functions if you would credibly pursue it; an unconvincing alternative gives the employer all the power
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you have a competing offer or credible alternative, your leverage is real — use it explicitly and anchor high.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If your BATNA is weak, invest in building one: run parallel processes, identify extension options, or explore other markets before negotiating.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you disclosed your current salary or named a specific salary number at any point in this process?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether information asymmetry has already been compromised; if you've named a number, the negotiation is partially anchored and strategy must shift
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Was the number you named above or below what they've offered? If below, you need to reframe using market data rather than trying to walk back your stated floor
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Good — maintain that asymmetry; prepare deflection scripts for when they ask again

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a competing offer from a company you would genuinely consider working for?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the most powerful negotiation lever is available and can be used credibly
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you mentioned it to the recruiter, and have you framed your target company as the first choice?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are there other processes in flight that could produce a competing offer before the current deadline?

diagnostic_questions.question: Has your current employer already paid for LMIA processing and legal fees on your behalf?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether the employer investment argument is available in a raise or retention conversation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Quantify the investment ($3,000–$6,000+) and determine whether it has been raised in prior compensation conversations; if not, it is a credible new data point for a raise ask.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The investment argument is unavailable; focus compensation conversation on market data and delivered contributions instead

diagnostic_questions.question: In a retention counter-offer scenario: what was the primary reason you considered leaving?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether a money-only counter-offer from the current employer will actually resolve the situation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If compensation was the sole driver, a retention counter may work — but get specifics on timeline and structure.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If role scope, growth ceiling, management, or culture were factors, a salary match does not address the underlying issue and the 80% within-12-months departure statistic becomes highly relevant.

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the promotion discretionary or criteria-based?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have anything concrete to hold the company accountable to, or whether you're dependent entirely on manager goodwill
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If criteria-based, get the specific criteria and timeline in writing before any comp discussion
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If discretionary, prioritize converting vague promises into written criteria before negotiating comp — otherwise the promotion itself is at risk of indefinite deferral

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the recruiter's current tone — collaborative or administrative?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the company still sees room to move or has shifted into closure mode
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If collaborative, one more ask is likely acceptable; the recruiter may still be advocating for you
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If administrative or matter-of-fact, treat the current offer as the ceiling and decide whether to accept

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the recruiter said 'this is best and final' — and have you asked about signing bonus separately?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you've exhausted only one lever (base) or tested all available ones — signing bonus often has a different budget and different answer
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you asked about signing bonus and were also told no: are there non-cash terms like remote work or start date that still haven't been addressed?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If you haven't asked about signing bonus yet: what specific amount would bridge the gap between the current offer and your target?

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the title you're being offered match the scope of work you'll actually be doing, and does it match equivalent roles at peer companies?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is being underleveled, which affects both immediate equity grants and long-term career trajectory at future employers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you confirmed whether the title is what would appear externally, and whether a title upgrade would trigger a comp band re-evaluation?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Push for a title that reflects the scope; use the framing 'the work you've described sounds like a [higher level] — can the title reflect that?'

diagnostic_questions.question: How long is the clawback period, and is it 12 months or longer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the company is using industry-standard terms or aggressive retention mechanics that suppress mobility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 12 months: standard, likely acceptable. Focus energy on structure and termination trigger language.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If 18–24 months: push back on period length first, then structure. Frame as 'industry standard is 12 months' and request alignment.

diagnostic_questions.question: What OEWS wage level would the offered salary classify you at under the post-2025 H-1B lottery system?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether there is an alignment between salary negotiation and immigration outcome — a Level I or II offer may be negotiable upward using the mutual lottery odds benefit as leverage
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If Level III or IV, confirm this in your negotiation framing as a shared benefit. If Level I or II, use the wage-weighted lottery argument explicitly to push for Level III classification.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the company is unaware of the wage-weighted lottery system, educating them may itself open a salary conversation that wasn't available before.

diagnostic_questions.question: When the company pushed back on your counter, what did you say and what was your tone?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is maintaining positive framing under pressure or letting frustration show; enthusiasm loss during negotiation is one of the most common and costly mistakes
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Did you reiterate excitement for the role before restating your ask, or did you lead with the counter?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Have you countered yet at all, or accepted the pushback as final?

diagnostic_questions.question: What level is the offer, and have you confirmed whether it is at the low, mid, or high end of that band?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is evaluating near-term comp or long-term career trajectory; a misleveled offer has compounding consequences
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Does the offered level match the scope and expectations described in the role?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: The candidate cannot accurately benchmark the offer or assess career progression potential without this information

diagnostic_questions.question: In which province is the role located — specifically, is it BC or Ontario?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines which legal framework applies to salary history questions and pay transparency obligations
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If BC: You are protected by the Pay Transparency Act and can explicitly decline to answer salary history questions by citing the law.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If Ontario or other provinces: Redirect salary history questions tactfully without citing statutory protection, as the legal basis is weaker

diagnostic_questions.question: What round of negotiation are you in — is this your first counter or have you already exchanged multiple rounds?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether to use a high round-number anchor or a precise research-backed number
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If this is round 1, use a round number anchor above your target.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If this is round 2 or later and both sides have narrowed, switch to a precise number to signal seriousness and research.

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you already told your employer you're considering leaving or received an external offer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you've permanently altered the employment relationship and what risks come with the current path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: You're now in retention negotiation mode — be clear-eyed about whether the root cause can be addressed, not just compensated
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You still have full optionality — decide whether to use the external offer as leverage internally or simply take it externally

diagnostic_questions.question: Where does this offer sit relative to the levels.fyi median for this role and level?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether market data supports continued negotiation or whether the offer is already at or above market
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If at or above median, your negotiating argument loses market-data support; focus on closing or non-cash levers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If below median, market data is your strongest anchor for continued negotiation

diagnostic_questions.question: For a promotion: did you discuss compensation before or after expressing acceptance of the new role?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether your leverage has already been spent — accepting the role emotionally before negotiating comp eliminates your primary bargaining chip
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If before: what market data do you have for the new title to anchor your counter?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If after: is there still an opening to reframe the conversation as 'aligning before we finalize' rather than renegotiating after acceptance?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you mapped your proposed start date against the company's review cycle and bonus pro-ration schedule?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is inadvertently starting at a time that defers their first performance review and bonus eligibility by months
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is there a start date within 2–4 weeks of your current target that would put you inside the current review cycle rather than the next one?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Ask HR explicitly: when does the fiscal year begin, when are reviews, and how is bonus pro-rated for someone starting at my proposed date?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is this signing bonus replacing unvested equity from your prior employer?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the stakes of a clawback are doubled — losing both the original unvested equity AND the replacement bonus in the same departure event
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Clawback protections become highest priority. The entire equity-replacement rationale collapses if a layoff claws back the replacement amount.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Standard clawback risk applies — focus on the four negotiation points without the elevated urgency of equity replacement risk

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you anchoring your counter to market data, or to what feels safe given your visa situation?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you are negotiating as a rational market participant or as a fear-managed applicant — the answer determines whether your counter has external validity or just reflects anxiety
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If anchored to market data (levels.fyi, H-1B disclosures), your counter is defensible and credible — proceed with confidence.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If anchored to personal comfort or fear, stop and research market comps for your role, level, and company before sending any counter.

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you negotiating only on base salary, or have you mapped out all the dimensions you could adjust?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate understands that negotiation is multi-dimensional and whether they know where company flexibility actually lives
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Which non-salary items have you already asked about — signing bonus, equity cliff, vacation, remote work, professional development budget?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Why not — do you believe those items aren't negotiable, or did salary seem like the highest-value target?

diagnostic_questions.question: For option grants specifically: what is the exercise window after leaving the company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the equity creates a golden handcuff that limits the candidate's future job mobility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 90 days: can you afford to exercise vested options out of pocket if you leave before a liquidity event?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate may be agreeing to equity terms that trap them financially without realizing it

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have a specific competing offer from a named company at a specific dollar figure, or only general market interest?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Distinguishes between leverage that will survive employer scrutiny and leverage that will collapse under a basic follow-up question
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Verify the competing employer's LMIA or GTS status before deploying the offer as leverage to ensure it is practically actionable, not just nominally attractive.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Without a specific competing offer, shift to market data anchoring strategy using Glassdoor Canada, Levels.fyi, and Government of Canada Job Bank rather than competing offer framing

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the company said 'this is our best and final offer' on base?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether to stop pushing on base and pivot to signing bonus or equity as separate negotiable levers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Ask specifically whether signing bonus is separately negotiable, framing it as bridging the first-year gap.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Continue the base negotiation — 'final' has not been declared so room likely still exists.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the internal transfer affect your unvested equity or bonus eligibility?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The total real compensation cost of the transfer beyond just base salary and promo clock
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Quantify the unvested equity value and bonus impact; negotiate transfer terms that account for this loss
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Confirm this explicitly in writing with HR before accepting — vague assurances are not binding

diagnostic_questions.question: Is your offer deadline real or manufactured by the company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have room to request an extension and use that time to generate competing offers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If the deadline is company-imposed, request an extension framed as needing time for a thoughtful decision
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If the deadline is tied to a genuine competing offer expiration, use it as urgency with the target company

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you negotiating 2–3 specific levers with clear rationale, or presenting a broad list of everything you'd like?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's negotiation posture signals principled asks or extraction-maximizing behavior, which affects recruiter and hiring manager goodwill
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Good — make sure each ask has a concrete framing (matching current package, role scope alignment, one-time vs. recurring cost) rather than just 'I'd like more'
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Prioritize ruthlessly to 2–3 levers; decide which matter most and which are true nice-to-haves you're willing to drop to close

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you received any verbal representations about the clawback terms from the recruiter that differ from the written contract?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is relying on informal assurances rather than contract language — a dangerous gap
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Get every verbal assurance put in writing as a contract amendment before signing. Verbal representations are not enforceable in most jurisdictions.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Good — but still read the actual clause language rather than inferring terms from the bonus structure or company reputation

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have written confirmation of H-1B sponsorship intent as part of the offer package?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the immigration component of the offer is real or informal — verbal commitments are unenforceable and leave you exposed if the company's circumstances or personnel change
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Confirm it specifies H-1B filing (not just OPT extension), the expected timeline, and names the immigration attorney or firm.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Do not sign until you have written confirmation — request it explicitly as a condition of acceptance and treat the absence of it as a yellow flag about execution capacity.

diagnostic_questions.question: Does this offer come with a deadline, and have you explicitly addressed it with the recruiter?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether there is an exploding offer dynamic in play, and whether the candidate knows they must explicitly request an extension rather than assuming it will be granted
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you stated clearly that the timeline doesn't work for you and asked for an extension?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: How much time do you have? Is this enough to run your decision process deliberately, or are you being implicitly pressured?

diagnostic_questions.question: Have you checked levels.fyi for the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentile total comp for your specific level and role at this company?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate has objective market data to anchor their counter-offer or is negotiating without a benchmark
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Where does the current offer fall in that range, and what percentile are you targeting?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate is likely to either anchor too low or make an ask that is not credibly supported by data

diagnostic_questions.question: Is your company in a growth and retention posture or a cost-reduction and downsizing mode?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether emergency retention budget exists and whether a market correction request will be taken seriously
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If growth mode, retention budget likely exists — you have more room to negotiate and request off-cycle adjustments
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If cost-reduction mode, even a strong business case may hit structural budget limits — factor this into whether to pursue external options more seriously

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the company know you're aware of H-1B portability rights and that you have real alternatives?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether you have implicitly ceded BATNA power by signaling lock-in — employers who believe you cannot leave will price comp accordingly, even if the legal reality is more flexible
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If you've signaled awareness of portability and alternatives, you're negotiating from a stronger position than most visa holders in the same situation.
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Consider whether your communication has inadvertently signaled desperation or lock-in — adjust framing to imply optionality without being adversarial.

diagnostic_questions.question: What justification have you given or are you planning to give for your counter-request?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate is using market-based framing (strong) or personal-need framing (weak), and whether they have a specific reason at all
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Is the reason tied to market data, your quantified impact, or personal circumstance? The first two are significantly more persuasive
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: You need a reason — requests without justification feel arbitrary; even a modest reason substantially increases acceptance rate

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you genuinely willing to walk away from this offer if the company does not meet your target number?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the negotiation is real or performative; the source states that the final close and firm counter only work if the candidate is actually willing to decline
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Then name a specific total comp target and hold to it through the negotiation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Adjust negotiation tactics accordingly; do not use the commitment close and do not make ultimatums you will not follow through on

diagnostic_questions.question: How many interview rounds has this company put you through, and how many people have they involved?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The company's sunk investment in your candidacy; more rounds and more interviewers means stronger pressure on their side to reach agreement, which is leverage you can use
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Have you internalized that they are highly motivated to close you — or are you still treating yourself as the supplicant in this transaction?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Are you early in the process? If so, focus on establishing fit before any comp discussion

diagnostic_questions.question: Does your resume or cover letter use any language that could be interpreted as requiring employer-side immigration action?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether work authorization framing is eliminating you at the screening stage before your qualifications are evaluated
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Rewrite to explicitly state: open work permit, any employer eligible, no sponsorship or filing required, PR pursued independently
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Confirm the positive framing is proactive and visible (bolded, near the top) rather than buried or absent

diagnostic_questions.question: How long is your PGWP, and when does it expire?

diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 3-year PGWP: you have time to be strategic about CRS optimization including French preparation and PNP research
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If 1-year PGWP: time is extremely constrained; prioritize CEC-eligible employment immediately and investigate bridge options

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you currently on OPT, STEM OPT, or do you need H-1B sponsorship now?

diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If OPT: confirm you can answer 'yes' to work authorization questions without flagging sponsorship yet
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If H-1B needed now: company must be an active H-1B sponsor — check USCIS public data before investing in interviews

diagnostic_questions.question: Who are you emailing — a hiring manager, a recruiter, or HR?
