community_misconceptions.misconception: PGWP holders don't need to explain their work status because any Canadian employer will know what an open work permit means
community_misconceptions.why_believed: PGWP is a well-known program in immigration circles and among internationally-educated candidates; it feels like common knowledge in their own community
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Many Canadian employers — including HR teams at tech companies — do not understand PGWP and default to treating any 'work permit' mention as a sponsorship requirement; PGWP holders must proactively educate with specific language
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates get filtered out at the recruiter screen stage despite being fully authorized to work, attributing low response rates to qualifications rather than framing
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: As a PGWP holder, I need an employer to 'sponsor' my work permit in Canada
community_misconceptions.why_believed: US-centric immigration discourse dominates international student online communities; the concept of employer-sponsored work authorization (OPT, H-1B) is deeply embedded in the mental model of anyone who went through or followed US processes
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: PGWP is an open work permit issued to the individual — it is not tied to any employer and requires no employer action whatsoever
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates disqualify themselves from jobs they are fully eligible for by triggering employer sponsorship filters, or they undersell their status in interviews
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Asking whether a company sponsors visas is legally risky or counts as national origin discrimination
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Candidates conflate employment discrimination law with work authorization questions; the phrasing feels like it could touch on protected characteristics
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Employers are legally permitted to ask about future sponsorship needs because it relates to work authorization, not national origin. Discriminating based on citizenship status is restricted, but asking about sponsorship requirements is lawful.
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who believe this avoid clarifying sponsorship early, delaying a necessary conversation and wasting interview cycles at non-sponsoring companies
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: You should tell employers upfront that you need visa sponsorship — it saves everyone time and shows you're honest
community_misconceptions.why_believed: International students are advised to be transparent about work authorization to avoid wasting time; this feels like professional courtesy and risk management
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Disclosing sponsorship need before the hiring manager is invested in you as a candidate triggers a filter; the informed approach is to establish interest and value first, then raise visa status on the call when a real conversation is already happening
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who open with visa disclosure are screened out before their skills are read; they interpret the silence as rejection of their skills when it was actually a reflexive sponsorship filter
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Going to a top-5 PhD program guarantees strong industry research job placement
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Program prestige is the most visible, legible, and socially validated signal — it's what rankings, parents, and peers reference; it feels like the safest bet
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Industry research placement correlates more strongly with advisor-level industry connections and internship pipeline than with program rank; top-5 students with disconnected advisors frequently end up in postdoc limbo
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Students invest in getting into the most prestigious program possible while neglecting advisor selection criteria that actually predict outcomes, resulting in strong credentials but weak industry placement
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: If my employer verbally promised H-1B sponsorship when I was hired, they are legally obligated to follow through
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Employment promises made during hiring feel binding — it mirrors how salary offers work, where a verbal offer creates a reasonable expectation; workers assume immigration commitments follow the same logic
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Verbal promises of H-1B sponsorship are not legally enforceable contracts; promissory estoppel claims are possible if there is written evidence and detrimental reliance can be proven, but are extremely difficult to litigate and rarely succeed
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Workers who rely on this belief delay finding a new sponsor, exhaust their OPT runway, and then face a compressed or impossible timeline to find a new H-1B sponsor before the next cap season
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: If my stock options are underwater (stock price below strike price), I simply don't exercise and I lose nothing
community_misconceptions.why_believed: For unexercised NSO options this is technically true — but it feels universally applicable to all option types
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: For ISO options that have already been early-exercised, AMT may have already been calculated on the spread at exercise time; if the stock subsequently drops, you still owe the AMT tax on a gain that no longer exists in the stock's current value
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Employees who early-exercise ISO options and then see the stock collapse face tax bills that can exceed the current value of their shares, and in extreme cases lead to bankruptcy
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Never show your bottom line — keep HR guessing to maximize your offer
community_misconceptions.why_believed: This advice comes from general negotiation theory where information asymmetry favors the side that reveals less
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: In hiring, HR cannot finalize or advocate for a salary internally without knowing candidate expectations — withholding this information stalls the process and reduces HR's ability to push for a higher number on your behalf
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: HR makes a conservative internal recommendation to hedge uncertainty, or the process stalls — in both cases the candidate ends up with a worse outcome than if they had stated their number clearly
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Options (期权) are real compensation and should be counted when comparing offers
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Recruiters present options as part of total comp; large projected values feel concrete even if unvested and contingent on liquidity events
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Options are 'big cakes' (大饼) in most cases — they should be excluded from your offer comparison calculation entirely; only count guaranteed, vested cash
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates accept lower base salary in exchange for options that never vest or never become liquid, ending up with less actual compensation
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: If you work hard and get good performance reviews, the company will eventually raise your pay to be equal to colleagues who started at a higher salary
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Managers and recruiters sometimes imply this during offer conversations to deflect negotiation; it feels meritocratic and fair — if you earn it, you'll get it
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Performance raises are applied as percentages of your current base within predefined bands. The same performance rating on a lower base produces a smaller absolute raise than on a higher base. The structural gap persists and often grows.
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who defer negotiation and rely on performance to correct the gap find themselves permanently underpaid relative to peers, with no internal mechanism to close it
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_收到_offer_后能重新谈吗.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Once you receive an offer, negotiating will almost certainly cause the company to rescind it or view you as a troublemaker
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The top answer on this post describes the manager's internal re-approval burden and the risk of being labeled a '刺头' (troublemaker), making the risk feel very concrete and personal
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Negotiation at the offer stage is standard practice and expected by HR; the cost of losing a good candidate over a modest salary gap is higher than the cost of adjusting the number. Multiple informed commenters with real hiring experience explicitly contradict the 'rescission risk' framing
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who believe this misconception silently accept below-market offers, leading to ongoing dissatisfaction, distraction, and eventual turnover — outcomes worse for both parties than the negotiation would have been
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: RSU share count is locked in at the time you receive your offer
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The offer letter specifies a dollar value which feels like a contract; candidates naturally assume the share count is also determined at that point
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Share count is calculated on the employee's first day of employment based on the stock price that day (or a recent rolling average per company policy); only the dollar value commitment is made at offer time
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who model compensation based on an assumed share count may be surprised — positively or negatively — when the actual share count is set at a different stock price
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: HR will give you a fair salary if you trust the process — no need to negotiate aggressively
community_misconceptions.why_believed: It feels confrontational to push back; many candidates want to appear agreeable and assume companies act in good faith on compensation
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: HR is optimizing for the company's budget, not the candidate's wellbeing; the opening offer almost always has negotiation room built in
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who don't negotiate leave 20–60% of achievable compensation on the table, according to the source
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Any full-time job in Canada for 1 year qualifies you for Canadian Experience Class
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The '1 year of Canadian work experience' requirement sounds simple and unconditional; the NOC TEER requirement is a technical detail not prominently discussed in casual community advice
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: CEC requires 1 year of work experience in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 — roles outside these categories (e.g., TEER 4 or 5) do not qualify
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: A candidate who works a full year in an ineligible role and applies for CEC will be refused, losing potentially their entire PGWP validity window with no PR pathway
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Being on F-1 OPT means you need employer visa sponsorship to work
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The word 'visa' creates confusion — candidates and recruiters alike assume any immigration status requires employer action; OPT's self-held nature is non-intuitive
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: F-1 OPT is authorized by USCIS and attached to the student, not the employer. The employer takes no sponsorship action for standard OPT. STEM OPT extension requires I-983 and E-Verify enrollment, which is minor relative to H-1B.
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates incorrectly answer 'yes' to sponsorship questions, triggering rejections that wouldn't have occurred if the distinction were understood; some recruiters also incorrectly screen out OPT candidates under a 'no sponsorship' policy
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Emailing HR or the careers inbox is the right way to do cold outreach
community_misconceptions.why_believed: HR and careers inboxes are the publicly designated job inquiry contacts; using them feels like following the correct process
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: HR screens on quotas and sponsorship flags; hiring managers engage to solve problems. For cold outreach, the hiring manager is the correct target
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Cold emails sent to HR enter the same filter as job board applications and yield similarly low callback rates; the candidate gets no benefit from the personalization of cold outreach
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: A PhD always pays off financially in tech because research scientist salaries are high
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Research scientist TC figures ($200-350K) are visible and cited frequently; the opportunity cost calculation over 4-5 years of foregone industry salary is less salient and rarely discussed
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: The PhD premium is real for research roles but minimal for SWE roles; for students who end up in SWE, the 4-5 year earnings gap ($150K+ vs $32K stipend) is rarely recovered
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Students pursue PhDs without a specific research career goal, lose years of compounding salary and equity, and enter SWE roles at the same level as peers who entered directly — at significantly higher total cost
community_misconceptions._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: RSU is safer than options because you don't have to pay anything to receive it
community_misconceptions.why_believed: RSU requires no upfront capital and vests automatically — it feels unconditionally positive
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: RSU vesting is a taxable event at ordinary income rates; for pre-IPO RSU, a large accumulated balance at IPO can create a massive single-year tax liability, and if the company's stock drops after IPO lockup expires, the employee has already paid taxes on a higher value than they can now recover
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Employees who receive large pre-IPO RSU grants, pay ~50% tax at IPO vesting, and then hold shares that subsequently decline end up with less net value than the headline grant suggested — sometimes significantly less
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Asking HR 'what do you think I'm worth?' is a clever tactic to get them to anchor high
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Candidates think this flatters HR into volunteering a high number, or at minimum avoids the candidate anchoring too low
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: HR commenters explicitly identified this as one of the most frustrating and counterproductive responses — HR cannot answer this question without a formal evaluation process, and the question signals that the candidate lacks self-awareness
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: HR forms a negative impression of the candidate's self-knowledge, which may reduce internal advocacy even if the technical interview went well
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Promised annual raise percentages should be factored into your offer comparison
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Companies present 'annual review with up to X% raise' as a benefit; it feels like a quantifiable future value
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Annual raise promises are non-guaranteed and vary by performance, company financials, and manager discretion; they should not be counted in your offer comparison
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Overvaluing one offer based on raise promises, then receiving minimal or no raises, while the competing offer's actual guaranteed compensation would have been superior
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Re-negotiating after receiving an offer signals bad faith and will get the offer rescinded or damage the relationship
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Stated confidently by the top answer; feels intuitive because the offer represents a completed internal process — pushing back feels like disrupting it
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Post-offer negotiation is standard practice in most professional and tech hiring markets. Employers expect it. The actual risk level depends on market context, how negotiation is framed, and whether a competing offer exists — not on the mere act of asking.
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who believe this forgo negotiation entirely at the offer stage, locking in a lower base with no path to correction
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_收到_offer_后能重新谈吗.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: If you negotiate and the salary can't be raised now, you can agree with the recruiter to get a raise after a successful probation period
community_misconceptions.why_believed: It feels like a reasonable compromise — prove yourself first, then get rewarded. Recruiters sometimes make this vague promise to close the hire
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Labor contracts lock in salary on signing; large companies have formal salary review cycles and cannot make ad-hoc adjustments outside them; informal verbal promises from recruiters are unenforceable and HR management will not honor them because it creates untracked budget variance
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: The candidate signs at a salary they are unhappy with, the informal promise is never honored, and they have no recourse — the optimal negotiation window has passed
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: When RSUs vest, you get to keep all the shares
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The vesting event feels like receiving a paycheck; the concept of shares being withheld for taxes is non-intuitive for people unfamiliar with equity compensation
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: RSU vesting triggers ordinary income tax; the company withholds a portion of the vested shares (typically 30-40%) and sells them to cover the estimated tax liability. The employee receives the remainder
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Employees who expect to receive 2,500 shares at vesting may actually receive ~1,500 shares; planning for large share accumulations or stock concentration management will be off if this is not understood
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Giving a wide salary range is safer because it gives you flexibility
community_misconceptions.why_believed: A range feels less committal and candidates think it avoids conflict while still conveying their general expectations
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Recruiters anchor to the bottom of any range you give; a range signals indecision and gives the employer a free anchor at your minimum
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidate gets offered the floor of their stated range or lower, having anchored the negotiation against themselves
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: The RSU or option value stated in your offer letter is your actual compensation
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The offer letter presents a specific dollar figure or share count, which anchors perception of total compensation
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: The stated value is pre-tax gross; actual take-home depends on tax bracket, state of residence, vesting schedule timing, stock price at vesting (for RSU), and whether the company achieves a liquidity event (for pre-IPO grants)
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates accept offers based on inflated perceived compensation, then experience sticker shock at the actual after-tax, post-liquidity-risk value they realize
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: If you underquote to get the job, you'll make it up in later raises and bonuses
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The HR commenter Hannah Han partially endorsed this view — saying hard workers will eventually be rewarded regardless of starting salary
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: While the HR commenter stated this reassuringly, the structural reality (acknowledged elsewhere in the thread) is that raises are anchored to current salary, pension contributions are calculated on base pay, and 'making it up later' requires both a good company culture and continued outperformance — none of which are guaranteed
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who accept below-market starting salaries often find the gap persists or widens; the reassurance that 'you'll be compensated later' is a risk transfer from employer to employee
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: The offer with the highest raw score across all factors is the right choice
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Summing scores feels rigorous and objective; people equate 'higher number' with 'better choice'
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Raw scores without personal importance weights are meaningless; the correct method multiplies each factor's score by its importance weight before summing
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Choosing the wrong offer — the worked example in the source shows raw scores favoring Offer A while weighted scores strongly favor Offer B
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Options are worse than RSUs because you have to pay to exercise them
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The requirement to spend money to exercise options feels like a disadvantage versus RSUs which are 'free'; the downside protection of options is non-intuitive
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: At failing companies, RSU holders have already paid ordinary income tax on vested shares that are now worthless — a real economic loss. Option holders can simply not exercise, losing only the opportunity cost. Options provide asymmetric downside protection that RSUs lack
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates at risky early-stage startups who discount option grants in favor of RSU grants may actually be accepting worse risk-adjusted compensation
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: You can negotiate salary only at the formal offer stage
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The offer stage feels like the 'official' moment for compensation discussion; earlier conversations feel premature
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Compensation framing begins at the first recruiter call when they ask about current salary and job-change motivation; the formal offer stage just confirms what was already established
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates who don't manage the comp framing early find the recruiter has already anchored internally to a number, making later negotiation much harder
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Bonus is paid in December at year end
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The term 'annual bonus' and 'year-end bonus' implies payment coincides with the calendar year end
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Annual bonuses in US tech companies are typically paid in January through March of the following year, so they are taxed as income in the year they are received (the new year), not the performance year
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Employees who plan to leave in December may miss their bonus entirely if they don't understand the actual payout timing; those who leave in January after receiving the bonus correctly capture it
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: HR's stated salary ceiling or raise-cap policy is a hard limit you cannot exceed
community_misconceptions.why_believed: The phrasing 'company policy' sounds official and non-negotiable; candidates don't want to appear unreasonable by challenging a stated rule
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: HR's stated ceiling is often their personal approval authority, not the company's true maximum; strong candidates can trigger a special approval process
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Candidates accept a below-potential offer when a special approval would have yielded their target number
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

community_misconceptions.misconception: Inflating your salary history slightly is a safe way to get a higher offer since it's hard to verify
community_misconceptions.why_believed: In the past, salary verification was rare; candidates assume the recruiter takes their word for it
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: Employers increasingly require bank statements, tax records, and original offer letters; background checks include HR-to-HR salary verification calls
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Fabrication is discoverable; if caught it results in offer rescission, contract termination, and potential industry blacklisting
community_misconceptions._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Internationally-educated candidate on PGWP, 3-month job search, Toronto/Waterloo market, no prior Canadian work experience
real_case_outcomes.decision: Shifted from cold-applying to large companies → attending local tech meetups → getting referrals → targeting mid-size companies; added explicit open work permit statement to resume and interview intro
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Weeks 1–4 (cold applications): 80+ applications, 2 phone screens. Weeks 5–8 (networking): 8 phone screens. Weeks 9–12: 4 onsites, 2 offers
real_case_outcomes.lesson: The combination of network-driven referrals AND explicit PGWP framing produced dramatically better outcomes than volume-based cold applications; both factors appear necessary, not just one

real_case_outcomes.situation: International graduate in Canada with PGWP completed the full 2-year post-graduation journey including job search, Express Entry pool participation, and PR approval
real_case_outcomes.decision: Shared the complete strategy publicly: framed PGWP correctly to employers, accumulated CEC-eligible experience, optimized CRS, and obtained PR
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Successfully obtained PR; post received 1089 upvotes indicating high community validation of the approach
real_case_outcomes.lesson: The PGWP-to-PR pipeline has a clear, reproducible sequence; success depends on understanding PGWP framing correctly from the start and treating CRS optimization as an active task rather than a passive one

real_case_outcomes.decision: Candidate explained they are currently on OPT and do not need sponsorship at this time
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Recruiter reversed their position and continued the process — the company's policy only applied to active petition sponsorship, not OPT
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Recruiter-stated 'no sponsorship' policies are frequently based on incomplete understanding of OPT; a calm, factual explanation of OPT's self-held nature can reopen doors that candidates assume are closed

real_case_outcomes.situation: International student on OPT, graduated May, two months of job board applications yielding no results
real_case_outcomes.decision: Switched to cold email outreach targeting hiring managers directly; kept emails under 100 words; asked only for a call; referenced specific work by the recipient; followed up on day 4 and day 9; did not mention visa status in the email
real_case_outcomes.outcome: 3 interviews and 1 job offer within 6 weeks of switching strategy
real_case_outcomes.lesson: For international students facing sponsorship-based filtering in job board and HR channels, cold outreach to hiring managers with delayed visa disclosure and low-commitment asks is a meaningfully higher-yield strategy

real_case_outcomes.situation: PhD students at a rank-20 program whose advisor had direct collaborations with OpenAI
real_case_outcomes.decision: Students leveraged the advisor's industry network for internships at the collaborating lab
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Received offers from OpenAI despite attending a non-top-5 program — outperforming peers from higher-ranked programs with less industry-connected advisors
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Advisor industry network is a stronger placement predictor than program rank for industry research roles; a rank-20 program with the right advisor can outperform rank-5 programs with disconnected advisors

real_case_outcomes.situation: Software engineer hired 18 months ago with verbal promise of H-1B sponsorship; now 9 months into STEM OPT (15 months remaining) after company rescinded sponsorship commitment due to 'policy change'
real_case_outcomes.decision: Original poster identified four options: find new H-1B sponsor, find cap-exempt bridge employer, pursue alternative status (L-1/O-1/marriage), or re-enroll in school on F-1; committed to getting any future sponsorship promise in writing
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Case was ongoing at time of post; a commenter in a similar situation reported finding a new sponsor within 8 months by being upfront about timeline in every interview

real_case_outcomes.situation: Employee joins a startup, receives NSO options with $5 strike price on 10,000 shares; company IPOs 4 years later at $25/share with all options vested
real_case_outcomes.decision: Employee exercises all 10,000 options at once in the IPO year, realizing $200,000 in gains
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Tax on $200,000 at ordinary income rates plus California state tax consumes approximately $100,000; plus $50,000 upfront exercise cost = $150,000 total outlay to net $50,000 from a $200,000 paper gain
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Exercising all options in a single year maximizes tax exposure; staggered annual exercise can reduce marginal rate and total tax burden — but requires planning before the IPO year

real_case_outcomes.situation: A candidate with 2 years of experience and a current salary of 5,000 CNY/month applied for an e-commerce operations role and stated an expected salary of 15,000 CNY/month — a 3x ask
real_case_outcomes.decision: The HR interviewer and hiring manager decided to interview him despite the unusual gap; he spent 2 hours demonstrating concrete operational value
real_case_outcomes.outcome: The hiring manager circled the 15,000 figure on his form and told HR to offer exactly that — the prior 5k salary became completely irrelevant
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Exceptional demonstrated ability overrides prior salary as an anchor entirely; the risk of quoting a high number is only that you don't get the interview — once you're in the room, your value is what determines the offer

real_case_outcomes.situation: Candidate comparing Offer A (higher pay, longer commute, less growth potential) vs Offer B (lower pay, shorter commute, faster promotion opportunity) using raw score totals
real_case_outcomes.decision: Initially appeared to choose Offer A based on raw total (390 vs 370)
real_case_outcomes.outcome: After applying weighted scoring with personal importance weights, Offer B scored 104 vs Offer A's 69 — a large reversal showing Offer B was the correct choice
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Weighted scoring can completely reverse a raw-score decision; never compare offers without applying personal importance weights calibrated to your own priorities

real_case_outcomes.situation: Experienced professional in Shanghai receiving job offers below salary expectations during two separate job changes
real_case_outcomes.decision: Consistently declined all offers where HR or headhunters said the compensation could not meet the stated expectation, without exception
real_case_outcomes.outcome: First job change resulted in a 100% salary increase; second resulted in a 50% increase
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Credible walkaway behavior — actually declining non-matching offers rather than capitulating — is what produces large compensation gains; the willingness to walk is the leverage, not the negotiation script
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Employee A joins Company X with 100K base + 100K RSU over 4 years (25K/year); two years later approaches the compensation review with no equity refresh granted
real_case_outcomes.decision: Employee did not ask about equity refresh at offer time and did not proactively negotiate for a refresh grant in performance reviews
real_case_outcomes.outcome: At the 2-year mark, the employee's forward-looking annual compensation drops from 125K to 100K for years 3-4, making any competing offer above 100K base financially attractive and giving the employer minimal retention leverage
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Equity refresh is a critical retention and compensation tool that must be proactively negotiated — both at offer time (ask about the policy) and at performance reviews (ask for a refresh grant). Ignoring it creates a self-inflicted compensation cliff

real_case_outcomes.situation: Candidate (小王) negotiated salary without disclosing full compensation details upfront; failed to mention 13th-month salary and various supplements during initial call
real_case_outcomes.decision: Let the recruiter issue an offer based on incomplete information, then tried to raise the 13th month, meal stipend, and transport allowance after the written offer was issued
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Recruiter became frustrated, offer re-approval was burdensome, recruiter began considering second-choice candidate; deal stalled with neither party advancing it
real_case_outcomes.lesson: All compensation components must be communicated proactively before the offer is issued — post-offer discovery attempts are perceived as bad faith and can kill the deal
