real_case_outcomes.situation: Students from top-5 programs with advisors who had no industry collaborations or internship pipelines
real_case_outcomes.decision: Chose advisors based on academic reputation and citation metrics without investigating industry connections
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Graduated into postdoc positions rather than industry research roles despite strong program prestige
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Program prestige alone does not substitute for advisor industry network when the target outcome is an industry research job; the internship pipeline is the mechanism that converts academic training into industry placement
real_case_outcomes._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Employee joins a startup early and receives ISO options; exercises early to start the capital gains clock before IPO
real_case_outcomes.decision: Early exercises ISO options at a low strike price, anticipating IPO and long-term capital gains treatment
real_case_outcomes.outcome: If the company's stock subsequently collapses (as happened widely in 2000), the employee still owes AMT calculated on the spread at exercise time — tax bills can exceed the current value of the shares, leading to bankruptcy in the most severe cases
real_case_outcomes.lesson: ISO early exercise is a high-stakes tax strategy that requires professional advice and a credible exit scenario; it is not a universally beneficial optimization and carries catastrophic downside
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Professional who left a job because internal approval processes were too bureaucratic, requiring multiple rounds of sign-off for even small initiatives
real_case_outcomes.decision: Resigned from the role despite presumably acceptable pay and team
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Left due to loss of autonomy and sense of achievement caused by process friction
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Decision-making autonomy (权利) is a factor that is hard to assess before joining but becomes a primary driver of resignation; candidates should explicitly investigate approval processes and decision-making latitude during interviews
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Candidate received an offer where salary had not been explicitly negotiated during interviews — only a rough range was discussed — in both a Chinese company and a US company
real_case_outcomes.decision: Proactively called/emailed HR after receiving the written offer: thanked them, reaffirmed interest, then explicitly raised compensation concerns with market data and benefit comparisons
real_case_outcomes.outcome: The negotiation was treated as normal by HR in both cases; the process described as standard by the US business school career office as well
real_case_outcomes.lesson: The written offer is the correct and expected trigger point for compensation negotiation; doing it by phone or email with a warm, professional framing and market-based justification is standard practice in both markets
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Silicon Valley employee leaves a company with significant vested ISO options; strike price is $1, current 409A valuation is $11, with 10,000 vested shares
real_case_outcomes.decision: Must decide whether to exercise 10,000 ISOs within 90 days of departure, requiring $10,000 cash outlay plus potential AMT exposure on $100,000 paper gain
real_case_outcomes.outcome: The author frames this as a genuine financial trap; employees who lack liquidity either forfeit the vested options or are forced to exercise under pressure without optimal tax planning
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Before leaving a company with vested options, calculate the full exercise cost (shares × strike price) plus potential AMT liability, and negotiate with the new employer to cover this cost via a sign-on bonus if possible — some Silicon Valley companies will fully cover this amount to secure the candidate
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Same candidate (小王, improved version) prepared a full compensation breakdown including 13th month, 3-year bonus average, and imminent pay raise; disclosed a competing offer during negotiations
real_case_outcomes.decision: Presented documented comp total of ~430k/year, argued for 55k/year target based on upcoming raise as base; later disclosed a competing offer at target level and expressed genuine preference for current company; asked for specific number (36k/month) to close
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Recruiter escalated to special approval process with hiring manager; candidate received 36k/month offer, above the initially stated ceiling of 35k
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Documented comp history, a competing offer, and a specific closing ask (not a range) together can unlock special approval processes that exceed stated HR ceilings
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Candidate (小陈) had a volatile bonus history — 1 month last year but 4 months average the two prior years
real_case_outcomes.decision: Headhunter presented a 3-year average compensation figure with supporting bank statements, requesting 10% above that average
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Employer offered 8% above the 3-year average — lower than the 10% ask but substantially higher than 15% above last year's actual comp would have produced
real_case_outcomes.lesson: When recent comp is anomalously low, anchoring the negotiation to a documented multi-year average is more effective than fighting over a percentage of the bad year
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

real_case_outcomes.situation: Friend of poster received initial max offer of 10k vs. expected 14k; company had pressing hiring need and candidate had 4+ years relevant experience with 80%+ role match
real_case_outcomes.decision: Candidate itemized specific differentials between old and new company benefits (social insurance contribution levels, absence of overtime pay), then mentioned a competing offer to create urgency
real_case_outcomes.outcome: HR called the next day and confirmed 14k offer had been approved
real_case_outcomes.lesson: Concrete benefit-differential arguments combined with competing offer leverage are more effective than simply restating a desired number; the combination triggers HR escalation
real_case_outcomes._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Sending 80+ applications and getting only 2 phone screens — interpreting this as a qualifications problem rather than a strategy or framing problem
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fundamental attribution error — attributing poor outcomes to fixed personal deficits (not qualified enough, foreign background) rather than correctable situational factors (wrong channel, wrong framing)
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates continue the same cold-application strategy for weeks, adding more applications rather than changing approach; or they downgrade target companies rather than fixing authorization language
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Audit the application funnel systematically: is the problem at the screen stage (framing/authorization language), the network stage (referral vs. cold), or the interview stage (skills)? The 2% response rate on cold apps is a channel problem, not a candidate quality problem.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International graduates in Canada who were in the US job market previously (or follow US-focused communities) defaulting to sponsorship language in Canadian applications
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Internalized identity as 'a visa burden' from the US context — a learned helplessness or self-labeling that persists even when the factual situation has changed
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Writing 'requires sponsorship' or adding visa caveats to Canadian job applications despite holding an open work permit that requires no employer action
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the identity explicitly: 'In Canada with a PGWP, you are not an international candidate from an employer's perspective — you are a domestic hire. Stop using language that marks you as something you are not.'
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International candidates describing their visa status in apologetic, hedging, or self-deprecating language before the company has raised any concern
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Anticipatory rejection anxiety — the candidate pre-emptively frames themselves as a liability to soften an expected rejection, rather than waiting to see if it is actually a problem
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Over-explains visa situation unprompted, uses qualifiers like 'I know this might be complicated,' avoids asking clarifying questions because the answer feels predetermined
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe visa status as a logistical data point, not a character flaw. High-voted comment captures it: 'Don't apologize. Don't hedge.' Coach candidates to state facts neutrally and ask questions confidently.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International student asks 'what do I say when they ask about sponsorship on the call?' — 267 upvotes on the question signal this is a widespread anxiety point
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of the sponsorship conversation as a binary rejection event; the candidate has avoided the topic in the email but now anticipates it as an unavoidable disqualifier on the call
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate freezes at the sponsorship question, over-explains, apologizes for the constraint, or fails to prepare a confident response — undermining the credibility they built in the email
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: by the time they ask about sponsorship on a call, they are already considering you — the question is not a disqualifier, it is a logistics check. Prepare a one-sentence, confident, factual answer: 'I'm on OPT now, which gives 12 months of authorization to start, and [company] has sponsored in the past for strong matches.' Practice it until it sounds like you're solving their problem, not apologizing for yours.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Choosing between PhD programs based heavily on rankings and prestige signals
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Prestige-seeking as risk reduction — the belief that choosing the most visible, socially validated option minimizes the chance of a bad outcome and provides defensible cover if things go wrong
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates focus almost exclusively on program rank and advisor h-index, avoid asking direct questions about internship placement during visits, and feel that a 'lower-ranked' program advisor with industry connections is a riskier choice
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect the candidate's risk frame: the actual risk is not 'lower prestige program' but 'no internship pipeline' — the advisor's placement record is the risk-reduction tool, not the ranking
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate receives a job offer and is asked to confirm acceptance — they need H-1B sponsorship language in writing but fear that pushing back will cause the offer to be rescinded
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Loss aversion combined with scarcity framing — the offer feels like a rare, fragile opportunity that will disappear if the candidate makes any demands
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts the offer without requesting written sponsorship language, rationalizing that 'the company seems reputable' or 'they mentioned it verbally so it's fine'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the written sponsorship request as standard due diligence, not a negotiation demand — 'I just want to make sure the offer letter reflects what we discussed about H-1B sponsorship so we're both on the same page.' This reduces the perceived confrontation and frames it as mutual clarity
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: New graduate receives an offer with equity and immediately asks 'how do I compare this to the other offer's salary?'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Certainty bias — the candidate anchors to the concrete, guaranteed component (salary) and discounts the variable component (equity) because it feels speculative and hard to evaluate
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate either ignores equity entirely in the comparison or treats the stated grant value as face-value equivalent to cash
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe equity as a range of outcomes, not a single number: 'Model three scenarios — company fails (equity = $0), company performs like peers (equity = stated value after tax), company outperforms (equity = 3-5x stated value). Now which offer looks better across scenarios?'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate refuses to state a salary number and says 'I care more about the platform and growth opportunities than salary'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of anchoring too low combined with imposter syndrome — the candidate lacks confidence in their market value and uses platform-framing as a face-saving deflection
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The candidate avoids any salary commitment, hoping the company will surprise them with a good offer — but comes across as either dishonest or lacking self-awareness to experienced HR
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the task: 'What is your market rate?' is not a trap — it is an invitation to advocate for yourself. Preparing a specific number backed by market data turns a fear-based deflection into a confident, informed answer.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Posting 'I have 3 offers, which is better?' without providing personal context, priorities, or situation
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Decision paralysis combined with externalized locus of control — the person wants someone else to make the decision for them to avoid ownership of the outcome
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asking strangers to compare offers by name alone, as if there is an objectively correct answer independent of the person's goals
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect: 'I can't answer that without knowing your core goal — what are you actually trying to get from this job in the next 3-5 years?' Force the person to own the priority-setting step before any comparison begins
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate asks whether they can re-negotiate after receiving an offer, framing it as a risk to the offer itself
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of losing the offer entirely — catastrophizing a normal professional exchange as a high-stakes threat
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts the first offer without pushback, or asks permission-seeking questions that signal they won't actually negotiate
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the question: the offer is not a fragile object that breaks if touched. Ask instead: 'What is my leverage right now, and what is the realistic downside of asking?' This separates perceived risk from actual risk.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_收到_offer_后能重新谈吗.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate asks 'will negotiating hurt my chances or make them think badly of me?' after already receiving an offer
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Fear of rejection and loss aversion — the offer feels like a fragile gift that could be taken away; asking for more feels like threatening the relationship
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts the first number without speaking, or asks tentatively and backs down immediately at any resistance
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: the offer is a non-binding proposal (要约), not a favor or a contract. You have made no commitment yet. Expressing counter-terms is the legally and professionally expected next step, not an act of ingratitude. HR's job is to close you within budget — they are on your side of this.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: First-time offer recipients asking 'is this offer good?' without specifying any components other than base salary
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Anchoring bias combined with information overload; the base salary is the most legible number so it becomes the proxy for total offer quality
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate evaluates and negotiates only the base salary, treating equity, bonus structure, and refresh policy as fixed background noise
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force a full compensation breakdown exercise: 'Write out base + expected bonus + year 1 RSU vest + 401K match. Now do the same for year 3 and year 4. Does your total comp hold up, or does it cliff?' This makes the multi-component structure visceral
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate says 'HR already said the maximum is X, I don't think it's possible to negotiate further'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Authority deference — treating an institutional-sounding statement as immovable fact; fear of appearing difficult or unreasonable
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate immediately accepts stated ceiling, abandons negotiation, and either accepts a below-market offer or walks away without trying
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe HR's ceiling as their personal authority limit, not the company's true maximum; explain that a strong candidate case gives HR the ammunition to escalate — your job is to provide that ammunition
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: PGWP expiration date creates time pressure that pushes candidates toward any available role rather than strategic targeting
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Scarcity mindset — perceived shrinking window triggers urgency that overrides strategic thinking, leading to higher-volume lower-quality application behavior
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates apply to roles they are overqualified for, expand to remote-only or US roles that don't actually help Canadian job search, or accept below-market offers without negotiating
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the timeline: a PGWP is typically 1–3 years; three months of searching is early-stage, not a crisis. Investing 4–6 weeks in network building before applications is time well spent, not time lost.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International graduates treating PR as a 'future problem' and focusing only on immediate job search
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Present bias and cognitive offloading — the urgency of job search crowds out planning for a deadline (PGWP expiry) that feels distant but is fixed and unforgiving
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: No language test booked, no NOC verification done, no CRS calculation attempted while actively job searching — then scrambling when the permit expiry approaches
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force the backward planning question: 'Your PGWP expires in X months. PR processing takes Y months. CEC requires 12 months of work. What does that mean you need to do this month?'
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate asks whether it is 'too late' to raise sponsorship after a technical interview but before the final round
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Decision paralysis combined with sunk cost avoidance — the candidate fears disrupting progress they've already made, so they defer the conversation further
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asking community whether they 'should' bring it up now or wait, framing the question as a timing dilemma rather than a required disclosure
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: 'Too late compared to what? The cost of not asking now is much higher — you'll have wasted a final round on both sides if sponsorship is a blocker.' Pre-offer is always the right window.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate reports 2 months of job board applications with no results and is considering giving up on job searching
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Attribution error: interpreting channel failure as personal failure; the candidate believes the rejections reflect their skills rather than a systematic filter that affects all international candidates applying through sponsorship-screening channels
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate continues the same failing strategy harder (more applications, more portal submissions) or becomes demoralized; does not consider that the channel itself is the problem
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: the data is about the channel, not about you. A 1% callback rate on job portals for international candidates is a structural outcome, not a personal one. The experiment is not 'am I good enough' — it is 'which channel bypasses the filter'.
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Considering a PhD when the actual career goal is a software engineering role
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Default path following — the PhD feels like the 'more' option, the safer hedge, or the signal that distinguishes candidates from the crowd, without a clear articulation of what specific outcome it enables
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidates say they want to 'keep options open' or 'go deeper' without specifying research roles; they avoid running the opportunity cost calculation explicitly
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force the specific role question: 'Name the exact job title you want in 5 years. Does that role require a PhD at the companies you're targeting?' — this breaks the vague optionality framing
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Worker discovers their employer has rescinded H-1B sponsorship with 15 months of OPT remaining
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Catastrophizing — the worker perceives the situation as an imminent status crisis rather than a solvable timeline problem, leading to paralysis or panic-driven poor decisions
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Fixating on worst-case outcomes (deportation, career loss) rather than methodically working through available options; potentially accepting a worse role or lower compensation just to secure any sponsorship quickly
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Force a concrete timeline audit: map exact OPT expiration, next H-1B cap registration date, and required job search lead time — transforming an amorphous fear into a specific deadline with actionable milestones reduces paralysis
psychological_barriers._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate at a pre-IPO startup asks 'should I take the lower base salary because the RSU is worth so much?'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Narrative bias — the candidate is seduced by the compelling startup story and assigns high probability to the optimistic liquidity scenario, underweighting the base rate of startup failures
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts below-market base salary in exchange for equity that may never liquidate, treating the RSU value as near-certain future cash
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask the candidate: 'If I told you today that this company will never IPO or be acquired, would you still take the offer at this base salary?' If no, the equity discount is larger than they're willing to accept
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate asks whether they should disclose their current (low) salary given that their expectation is much higher
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Shame about current compensation level combined with fear that disclosure will cap the offer — the candidate treats past salary as a verdict on their worth rather than a starting point
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate either lies about current salary or refuses to disclose it, creating verification risk and signaling untrustworthiness
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Disclose accurately and immediately shift the frame: 'My current salary is X, and based on my market research and the value I can bring to this role, I'm targeting Y.' This separates the factual anchor from the aspirational one.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Framing the offer choice as a binary between a higher-salary and a lower-salary option with no other dimensions mentioned
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Salary anchoring bias — salary is the most visible and easily comparable dimension, so it crowds out all other factors in the mental model
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: The person reduces a multi-dimensional decision to a single number comparison, treating salary as a proxy for total offer quality
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Expand the frame: 'Salary is only one of six dimensions. What role type is each offer? What company prestige? What team? Your salary in 5 years depends far more on those than on the current number.'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate says 'I'll just show them what I can do first, then ask for more after probation'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Sunk cost pre-commitment combined with hope bias — believing future performance will create a negotiation opportunity that doesn't structurally exist
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate signs a below-market offer, joins the company, discovers salary review windows are rigid and informal promises evaporate, and is stuck for 12+ months
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Ask directly: 'Can you show me where in the employment contract the post-probation adjustment is documented?' If it is not in writing in the offer letter, it does not exist. The negotiation window is now, not later.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: International students (F-1/OPT) asking whether they can negotiate at all given visa dependency on the employer
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Catastrophizing: the student perceives any negotiation as risking offer rescission, which conflates with visa status loss — a disproportionate fear response
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Student accepts first offer without negotiating any component; may not even ask clarifying questions about equity structure for fear of appearing difficult
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe the risk: 'Companies spend $20K–$30K recruiting you. Rescinding an offer for asking a reasonable compensation question has almost never been documented. The risk of not negotiating is guaranteed undercompensation; the risk of negotiating is near-zero.' This recalibrates the probability assessment
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate says 'the job market is bad right now, I should just take what they give me'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Scarcity mindset and catastrophizing — overweighting the risk of losing the offer relative to the benefit of negotiating
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts the first offer without negotiating, even when the company clearly needs them and has flexibility
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Point out that by the offer stage the company has already invested significantly in the candidate; the cost of restarting the search is real for them too — the candidate has more leverage than they feel they do
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Employee holds unexercised vested options after IPO and repeatedly defers the decision to exercise
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Regret aversion combined with status quo bias — exercising locks in a tax bill and feels like a commitment; not exercising feels like preserving optionality, even as the window to act shrinks
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Employee delays exercising year after year, misses optimal tax planning windows, and either forfeits options at expiration or exercises all at once in a high-tax year
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reframe: 'Every year you don't partially exercise, you are making an active bet that the stock will rise enough to justify a higher tax bracket hit later. Is that bet intentional or just inertia?'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate accepts a below-expectation offer immediately without counter-offering, citing fear of seeming difficult or losing the offer
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Scarcity mindset — treating any offer as a gift that could be taken away, rather than as a mutual transaction where both parties have leverage
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate says yes immediately or says 'I'll take whatever you can offer' — leaving money on the table and often feeling resentful afterward
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Remind the candidate: HR has already decided to make an offer, which means they want you. The negotiation at this point is low-risk — a reasonable counter rarely causes an offer to be rescinded. State the counter once, clearly, with a rationale.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Expressing fear of 'choosing wrong and regretting for life' when comparing job offers
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Loss aversion and catastrophizing — treating a reversible career decision as permanent and existentially high-stakes
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Paralysis, over-analysis, seeking external validation, delaying a decision beyond the offer deadline
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize reversibility: 'Every job is a stepping stone. The question isn't which offer is perfect — it's which offer gives you better options for your next move. You can course-correct.'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Fresh graduate (应届生) who feels they have no leverage and treats any salary as 'take it or leave it'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Status anxiety and imposter syndrome — believing their inexperience disqualifies them from having preferences or making asks
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Accepts first offer without any negotiation, sometimes even expressing gratitude for a below-market number
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Even fresh graduates have negotiable dimensions: start date flexibility, signing bonus, professional development budget, equity cliff timing. The ask does not have to be base salary. Negotiating one dimension builds the muscle and sometimes opens the door to others.
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidates who feel overwhelmed by equity complexity and say 'I'll just focus on the base salary since I understand that'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Complexity aversion leading to motivated reasoning — the candidate avoids the equity analysis because it's cognitively demanding, not because it's unimportant
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate systematically underweights or ignores equity in compensation comparisons, leading to choices that favor simpler (often lower total comp) offers
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Reduce the equity calculation to a single number: 'Annual equity value = total grant ÷ 4 (for standard vesting). Add that to your base. Now compare.' Make the calculation trivially simple to overcome the avoidance
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate feels excitement and relief at receiving an offer and wants to close quickly to avoid risking it
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Loss aversion activated by finally having an offer in hand — fear that any push-back will cause the offer to be rescinded
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate accepts immediately without counter-offering, or makes a token counter well below their actual target
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Normalize the expectation that negotiation is standard and expected; a well-framed counter virtually never results in offer rescission — recruiters build in buffer precisely because they expect negotiation
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate receives an offer below their target and asks 'should I just accept? I don't want to rock the boat'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Conflict avoidance — discomfort with assertiveness framed as pragmatism
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate frames accepting a below-target offer as 'being realistic' rather than acknowledging they are avoiding a difficult conversation
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Separate the emotional discomfort from the financial stakes; provide a script so the candidate only needs to repeat prepared language rather than improvise under pressure
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

psychological_barriers.trigger: Candidate hesitates to mention a competing offer because it 'feels dishonest' or 'too aggressive'
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Social norm violation anxiety — fear that using leverage will be perceived as manipulative or will damage the relationship with the recruiter
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Candidate withholds their strongest piece of leverage out of politeness, leaving thousands on the table
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Frame competing offers as market information, not threats — 'I want to be transparent that I'm evaluating another opportunity, and I'd prefer to be here, but I need the numbers to make sense'
psychological_barriers._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to apply to as many jobs as possible to maximize my chances of getting a Canadian tech role on PGWP
reframing_moves.reframe: Your bottleneck is not application volume — it is network access and authorization framing. Fix those two things and a smaller number of applications will outperform 10x the volume
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from a quantity optimization mindset to a conversion rate optimization mindset, which is the correct mental model given the documented 2% vs. 30% response rate differential
reframing_moves.example_language: Response rate jumped from ~2% to ~30% when I started asking people I met to refer me
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm an international student in Canada — I need to find an employer who will sponsor my visa
reframing_moves.reframe: You have a PGWP. That means there is nothing for an employer to sponsor. You are already authorized to work for any employer in Canada.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate's self-concept from 'liability requiring employer action' to 'unrestricted worker' — this changes the emotional posture and the literal language used in applications
reframing_moves.example_language: 'PGWP is genuinely not a burden to employers' — the framing should match the reality
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm worried about how to bring up my visa situation without it hurting my chances
reframing_moves.reframe: Your visa situation is a logistical fact, not a confession. State it plainly and ask directly — the anxiety in your delivery causes more damage than the visa status itself
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the locus of control from external (company's reaction to visa) to internal (candidate's delivery and confidence); reframes disclosure as neutral information exchange rather than a vulnerability
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Don't apologize. Don't hedge.' — the anxiety around this question makes candidates come across worse than the actual visa situation warrants
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to tell them I need sponsorship upfront so I don't waste their time or mine
reframing_moves.reframe: By the time you've had a conversation, the person is invested in you. Opening with 'I need sponsorship' immediately triggers rejection before they even read your skills.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from thinking about transparency as an obligation to thinking about sequencing as a strategy; the question is not whether to disclose but when — and timing changes the outcome entirely
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Opening with I need sponsorship immediately triggers rejection before they even read your skills.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Which PhD program should I choose for an industry research career? (implicitly focused on ranking and prestige)
reframing_moves.reframe: The real question is not which program — it's which advisor, and specifically: does this advisor have an active internship pipeline to your target companies?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate's evaluation unit from a visible, legible macro signal (program rank) to the actual causal mechanism (advisor industry network) — making the decision more actionable and predictive
reframing_moves.example_language: Ask during visits: 'Where did your students intern? Which ones ended up at industry labs?' That's the signal.
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My company broke their promise — what are my legal options and how do I fight this?
reframing_moves.reframe: Verbal promises aren't legally binding; the real question is how to use your remaining OPT time efficiently to find a new sponsor before the next cap deadline
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the poster from a retrospective legal framing (where they have almost no leverage) to a forward-looking timeline management framing (where they have significant agency), unblocking action
reframing_moves.example_language: VERBAL PROMISES AREN'T LEGALLY BINDING FOR H-1B... My only claim would be promissory estoppel which is hard to prove and even harder to litigate
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: New graduates focus on base salary differences and treat equity as a bonus or afterthought
reframing_moves.reframe: In Silicon Valley, the prevailing view is that equity is the primary wealth-building mechanism and base salary is just 'enough to live on' — the real question is the quality and structure of the equity
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate's optimization target from the certain-but-capped variable (salary) to the uncertain-but-uncapped variable (equity), prompting them to actually analyze the equity terms
reframing_moves.example_language: 硅谷、湾区的主流观点早就认为收入中股票期权为王，基本工资用来养养家就好
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How do I strategically avoid revealing my salary expectations so HR can't lowball me?
reframing_moves.reframe: HR cannot advocate for you internally without knowing your expectations — withholding this information doesn't protect you, it handicaps the person trying to get you more money
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from an adversarial frame (HR vs. me) to a structural one (HR as intermediary who needs my input) — changes the optimal behavior from concealment to clear communication
reframing_moves.example_language: HR在完全不了解候选人期望的前提下就和用人部门确定了薪酬，如果那个数字与候选人预期有较大差距，这次录用就只能以失败收尾了
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Which offer pays more / which company is bigger?
reframing_moves.reframe: Which offer gives you better long-term earnings trajectory, not just the highest number today?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the comparison from a static snapshot (current salary) to a dynamic model (career capital, role market value, company as resume credential), which is the actual variable that matters over a career
reframing_moves.example_language: 你的核心诉求是长期，稳定，可增长的钱，而非短期支票 ('Your core need is long-term, stable, growing income — not a short-term check')
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Can I still negotiate after receiving an offer, or is it too late / too risky?
reframing_moves.reframe: This is not the last chance to ask — it is the ONLY chance. Once you sign and join, you are on the boat and the boatman sets the terms. The offer stage is the single moment when you and the employer have roughly equal power.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the question from 'is it acceptable to ask?' to 'if not now, when?' — which reveals that waiting is not a safer option but actually the highest-risk move
reframing_moves.example_language: 见过艄公行船到江心敲乘船的竹杠，可没见过乘船的到了江心问艄公讨自己船票钱的 (You've seen the boatman raise prices at midstream — you've never seen a passenger demand a refund at midstream)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: How much is my RSU worth?
reframing_moves.reframe: Your RSU grant is a dollar commitment, not a share commitment — and the after-tax value is what you actually receive. Model it as: (vest value at that day's price) × (1 - your marginal tax rate) = actual shares/cash received
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from treating equity as a fixed asset to treating it as a variable cash flow with tax drag — a more accurate mental model that prevents both over- and under-valuation
reframing_moves.example_language: 当你vest RSU时，那笔收入是算作个人基本工资收入类别上税的，假设你个人税率是40%, 你实际收到的是60%的价值
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'My current salary is low, so I don't deserve a big raise' or 'HR is using my current salary as the baseline'
reframing_moves.reframe: Your current salary reflects what you were worth when you joined that company years ago — it does not reflect what your current experience is worth on the market today
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Separates historical accident (underpaid entry) from current market value; shifts the anchor from a number that disadvantages the candidate to one grounded in what the role actually requires
reframing_moves.example_language: 'My current salary reflects my compensation 3 years ago when I joined; my growth since then is not captured in that number, and it is already below market average'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Canadian employers will figure out what my work permit means — I shouldn't have to over-explain it
reframing_moves.reframe: Your job is not to be right about what employers should know — your job is to remove every possible reason for them to say no before they read your qualifications
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts responsibility for outcome from the employer's knowledge to the candidate's communication, which is the only variable the candidate can actually control
reframing_moves.example_language: I literally put 'Open Work Permit — no sponsorship needed' in bold at the top of my resume after getting confused looks from recruiters
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_getting_your_first_canadian_tech_job_on_pgwp_what_.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I just need to get a job first, then I'll figure out PR later
reframing_moves.reframe: Your PGWP has a fixed expiry. PR has minimum time requirements. These are not separate problems — they are a single constrained timeline you need to map now.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a vague future concern into a concrete backward-planning problem with specific milestones, making inaction visibly costly rather than abstractly risky
reframing_moves.example_language: The goal is: get job with PGWP → accumulate 1 year Canadian experience → maximize CRS score → get ITA → PR
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestionsCAD_pgwp_job_search_reality_check_what_nobody_tells_yo.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: The company said 'no sponsorship' so I can't apply there
reframing_moves.reframe: Find out what they actually mean by 'no sponsorship' — that phrase often means no H-1B petition, not no OPT, and many recruiters don't know the difference
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts a binary rejection into a diagnostic question; shifts candidate from passive acceptance of ambiguous language to active clarification that may reopen the opportunity
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Worth clarifying what they mean by no sponsorship' — some companies that say this will still do STEM OPT extension forms
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_asking_about_visa_sponsorship_in_job_interviews_th.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I should ask for a job in my cold email so the person knows what I want
reframing_moves.reframe: You're asking for a low-commitment 20 minutes. Every ask is for the next small step only.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces a transaction framing (ask for the thing you want) with a relationship sequencing framing (ask for the smallest yes that opens the next door); reduces the psychological barrier for the recipient to say yes
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Every ask is for the next small step only.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I get a PhD to improve my career in tech?
reframing_moves.reframe: The PhD has a strong premium for research roles and near-zero premium for SWE roles — the question is which of those you're actually targeting
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the assumption that the PhD is universally beneficial and forces a specific career goal articulation, converting an abstract credential question into a concrete ROI calculation
reframing_moves.example_language: The PhD premium is real for research roles; it barely exists for SWE roles.
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_industry_phd_vs_academic_phd_in_cs_ml_the_real_dif.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to find a new job that will sponsor my H-1B — how do I approach interviews without scaring employers away by mentioning visa status?
reframing_moves.reframe: Disclosing your visa timeline upfront isn't a liability — it's an efficient filter that saves you both time and concentrates your search on employers who are actually viable
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Converts the perceived weakness (visa disclosure = rejection risk) into a search efficiency tool, reducing the anxiety that drives candidates to hide their status and waste time on non-viable opportunities
reframing_moves.example_language: The key was being upfront in interviews: 'I'm on STEM OPT and need H-1B sponsorship by [date].' Honest screening saves everyone time.
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_my_employer_said_they_d_sponsor_h_1b_then_rescinde.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Employees assume equity is free upside with no downside — 'worst case I get nothing'
reframing_moves.reframe: The real worst case is not zero — it is a tax liability that exceeds the current value of your shares, as happened to thousands of engineers in 2000
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Replaces the comfortable 'free lottery ticket' mental model with an accurate risk model that includes negative outcomes, motivating due diligence on tax mechanics before acting
reframing_moves.example_language: 知道为啥2000年互联网大泡沫后无数程序员破产么？税！
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My current salary is low — if I reveal it, they'll only offer me a small increase
reframing_moves.reframe: Your current salary is a reference point, not a ceiling — what actually determines your offer is demonstrated ability and market rate, and these can be completely disconnected from your history
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the cognitive link between past salary and future offer, freeing the candidate to negotiate based on value rather than defending a prior anchor
reframing_moves.example_language: 之前的5k变得没有任何意义，也没有任何人再去关注这个数字
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I can't decide between these two offers — can you help me choose?
reframing_moves.reframe: Before comparing offers, you need to clarify your core need — without that, no framework will give you the right answer
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces the person to take ownership of their own value hierarchy before applying any evaluation tool; prevents borrowing someone else's framework that doesn't match their situation
reframing_moves.example_language: 同一个Offer，对不同的人来说，是完全不同的意义 ('The same offer means completely different things to different people')
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I don't want to seem greedy or cause problems for the hiring manager by asking for more
reframing_moves.reframe: Meeting recruiter targets within budget is the HR's KPI — not yours. Your job is to represent your own interests. The candidate who silently accepts a bad deal and then underperforms or leaves in 6 months is far more costly to the company than the candidate who negotiated up front.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Depersonalizes the negotiation — it reframes it as two professionals doing their respective jobs, removing the guilt and the feeling of imposing on someone
reframing_moves.example_language: 你的利益，自己不捍卫，别人犯得着多发你钱吗？(Your interests — if you don't defend them yourself, why would anyone else pay you more?)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: My offer says 100K base + 100K RSU over 4 years, so I'll make 125K per year
reframing_moves.reframe: That's only true for the first two years. What does your compensation look like in year 3 and year 4 — and is there an equity refresh? Without it, you're projecting a future pay cut
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces the candidate to think in a forward trajectory rather than a static annual snapshot, revealing the compensation cliff that is invisible in naive year-1 analysis
reframing_moves.example_language: 假设A接了Offer并在X公司开开心心地奋斗了两年，有一天突然意识到那时自己未来四年每年的收益为 (125k, 125k, 100k, 100k)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'They promised good bonuses and growth opportunities, so maybe the lower base is okay'
reframing_moves.reframe: Future bonuses are future value you will create then — they are a separate question from what your current experience is worth today
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces a clean separation between present compensation for present skills versus future compensation for future performance; prevents the candidate from discounting certain present-value dollars for uncertain future ones
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Future raises represent the extra value I create after I join; what we're negotiating now is what my existing experience is worth — those are two different questions'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: HR is the right contact for job inquiries because that's their job
reframing_moves.reframe: Managers hire because they have a problem to solve. HR screens because they have quotas. Very different conversations.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reframes the contact choice from a procedural question (who handles jobs?) to a motivational question (who is motivated to hire me?); changes who the candidate targets and why
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Managers hire because they have a problem to solve. HR screens because they have quotas.'
reframing_moves._source: cscareerquestions_cold_email_got_me_my_job_actual_template_that_work.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Pre-IPO startup equity feels real because the offer letter states a specific dollar value
reframing_moves.reframe: Equity at a pre-IPO company is contingent on two independent events happening: the company achieving a liquidity event, AND you still being an employee (or having exercised options in time). Until both occur, the value is zero.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the single-number anchor and replaces it with a two-condition probability model, forcing the candidate to separately assess both the company's exit probability and their own tenure probability
reframing_moves.example_language: 无论是RSU/Option, 只要公司没有办法上市或者被收购，或者你在此之前已经离开，这些RSU/Option则分文不值
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_受限股票单位_RSU_与股票期权_Stock_Option_的区别有哪些.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I should ask HR what they think I'm worth, so I don't anchor too low
reframing_moves.reframe: Asking HR to value you signals that you don't know your own value — the person who should know what you're worth is you, because you're the seller and sellers set the asking price
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Uses the buyer-seller market analogy to make it intuitive why the candidate (seller) should name the price first — removes the feeling that stating a number first is a weakness
reframing_moves.example_language: 在一对一的谈判过程中，最有效率也最合理的方式一定是卖方先出价，因为卖方最清楚自己的能力和价值
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_应聘时何时适合谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Should I go to the big company or the small company?
reframing_moves.reframe: Which option increases your career capital (experience value, role market price, resume credential) faster?
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the false binary of 'big = safe/good, small = risky/bad' and replaces it with a growth-rate comparison that accounts for stagnation risk at large companies
reframing_moves.example_language: 逆向思维，你希望你的简历上出现什么经验？你觉得哪个offer带来的经验更有含金量？ ('Reverse-engineer: what experience do you want on your resume? Which offer's experience is worth more?')
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: I'm not happy with the salary but I'll accept and prove myself, then ask for a raise after probation
reframing_moves.reframe: The satisfaction you expect to feel after 'proving yourself' will not arrive — it will be replaced by the same dissatisfaction, now with additional switching costs making it harder to leave. Unresolved dissatisfaction does not fade; it festers.
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Forces the candidate to think about the trajectory of accepting, not just the immediate relief of avoiding a difficult conversation
reframing_moves.example_language: 一旦有某些点触动到你，心里会更加难受 (Once something triggers you, the feeling only gets worse — it doesn't fade)
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_收到offer了还能不能再谈薪资.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: Options are risky because I have to pay for them, while RSUs are free
reframing_moves.reframe: RSUs are not free — you pay income tax on them at vest. If the company fails after you vest RSUs, you've permanently overpaid taxes on worthless shares. Options let you choose not to exercise, so your downside is zero. The question isn't 'which one costs money' but 'which one has better risk-adjusted value at this company's stage'
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Corrects the framing error by making the tax cost of RSUs visible and introducing the concept of optionality value — changing the decision axis from 'which requires cash' to 'which has better expected value given company risk'
reframing_moves.example_language: 如果是持有RSU的员工，因为RSU grant时已经交了一波个人所得税，公司倒闭时这些RSU就一文不值了，意味着她凭空多交了那么多个人所得税
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_求问美国it公司的rsu和bonus是怎么回事.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'The company's policy is a maximum 10% raise, so I can only push within that range'
reframing_moves.reframe: The percentage is not the constraint — the base the percentage is applied to is the constraint; change the base and the same percentage yields a very different number
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the false assumption that accepting the percentage framing means accepting the employer's preferred base; opens up a new axis of negotiation
reframing_moves.example_language: 'If we apply 10% to my salary as it will be after next month's internal adjustment, the number looks quite different from applying it to today's below-market figure'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: The higher-scoring offer in total points is obviously better
reframing_moves.reframe: Raw scores without weights are meaningless — the same offer scored by two different people with different priorities should produce different outcomes
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the false objectivity of raw totals and introduces the necessary step of personal values calibration, which is where the real decision actually lives
reframing_moves.example_language: 打分需要按照你自己的想法来，不需要参考别人的分数 ('The scoring must reflect your own judgment — you don't need to reference anyone else's scores')
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_接到了不同的_OFFER_应该怎么比较.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I need to convince HR to give me more money'
reframing_moves.reframe: You need to give HR the ammunition to go to their manager and fight for you — your job is to make their internal case as easy as possible
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the candidate from an adversarial 'demanding' posture to a collaborative 'enabling' posture; aligns the candidate's interest with the recruiter's interest in closing the deal
reframing_moves.example_language: 'Here is the documentation of my current comp and market data — I hope this gives you what you need to make the case internally'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt

reframing_moves.original_framing: 'I should ask for a range to seem flexible and reasonable'
reframing_moves.reframe: Giving a range means you have already named your floor — the recruiter will anchor to it and call it your expectation
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Reveals the hidden cost of appearing 'flexible'; transforms the candidate's instinct for politeness into a concrete numerical disadvantage they can see clearly
reframing_moves.example_language: 'A range just tells them the lowest number you'll accept — give them one number, the right one'
reframing_moves._source: zhihu_面试时谈薪的技巧有些什么啊.txt
